Cummins India (KKC) attracted a wide spread of views following its strong Q4FY26 results. **Jefferies** (Buy, PT ₹7,100) and **Geojit** (Buy, PT ₹6,160) anchor the bull end, with the thesis resting on data centre (DC) generator demand as a structural growth driver and electronic engine indigenisation post-CPCB IV+ upgrade boosting margins. The **neutral cluster** — **Nomura** (PT ₹6,000) and **JPMorgan** (PT ₹5,882, freshly downgraded from OW) — concedes the fundamentals are solid but sees risk-reward as balanced at current multiples; JP explicitly called out the strong run as "priced in." The bear camp — **Kotak** (Reduce, PT ₹5,600, downgraded from ADD) and **IDBI** (Sell, PT ₹5,046) — flags valuation excess and, in Kotak's case, structural market-share loss in non-HHP powergen that the DC story is partially masking. **PL** (Aug-2025 Hold, PT ₹3,895) and **ICICI** (Feb-2025 Hold, PT ₹2,900) are too stale to be actionable. The real debate: is DC demand a durable rerating catalyst or a lumpy, customer-concentrated tailwind that props up a business with competitive erosion in its core domestic genset segment?

My own read: Cummins India is a genuinely high-quality franchise — dominant in industrial power generation with a captive parent technology pipeline and pricing power that peers cannot easily replicate. But the DC tailwind, while real, is being weighted too heavily by the bulls. Kotak's flag on non-HHP powergen share loss deserves more scrutiny: if CIL is ceding ground in its core domestic genset market to Kirloskar and others, DC revenue can only compensate for so long — and DC capex is lumpy. Management's own May-2026 guidance confirmed margin headwinds persist, which sits uneasily with the Jefferies thesis of imminent margin recovery via indigenisation. At current multiples, the margin of safety is thin. I'd be in the neutral-to-cautious camp: own it for the franchise quality, but resist chasing at the top of the target range. The two things I'd watch most are (1) DC contribution sustaining above 15% of consolidated sales and (2) whether margin headwinds abate by Q2FY27 — if not, the Jefferies PT of ₹7,100 is difficult to defend.

Jeff|260529.change: PT raised ₹4,975→₹7,100; Buy (prior rating not captured in library).
Jeff|260529.view:
Jefferies is the most bullish house by a wide margin and carries the highest PT at ₹7,100. The call rests on three structural levers: electronic engine indigenisation post-CPCB IV+ (lifting margins), rising distribution segment mix, and DC revenue compounding from a ~13% base. The 5–7% EPS upgrades for FY27–28E reflect genuine fundamental revision, not just rerating.

The risk: at ₹7,100 Jefferies is embedding significant DC growth that must compound materially from current levels. DC buildouts are lumpy and customer-concentrated; a pause in hyperscaler capex would put a large dent in this PT. Worth holding from lower levels; adding fresh requires more evidence that DC ordering velocity is sustained, not a pull-forward.

JP|260531.view:
JPMorgan's downgrade is the most credible near-term caution in the pack — not a fundamental bear thesis but a clean valuation call: the stock has re-rated strongly and expected returns from here are modest. Raising the PT to ₹5,882 (Sep-27) while cutting to Neutral implies single-digit upside, which makes OW indefensible.

I think JPMorgan is right that the easy part of the trade is behind us. Their mention of Middle East top-down risks is worth tracking — CIL's export business and India's industrial capex cycle could both soften if the macro deteriorates. Neutral is the honest rating here, and it deserves weight precisely because JP was bullish before and has now changed their mind on the risk-reward.

Kotak|260530.view:
Kotak is the most structurally sceptical of the active houses, and their concern is the most underappreciated. Raising the PT while downgrading to Reduce signals that the stock's re-rating has outrun fundamentals — DC is priced, and the non-HHP powergen market-share loss is a real competitive worry that the DC story is obscuring.

Kotak's comparison to ABB and Siemens on DC 'salience' is pointed: as DC becomes proportionally larger, risk concentrates in a segment that is cyclical and customer-lumpy. REDUCE is the sole sell-side negative rating in this group, which historically makes it the call worth stress-testing. I think the market-share point in core gensets is correct and underweighted by the bulls.

Nomura|260601.view:
Nomura is the steadiest hand in the group — no new conviction, no rerating, just confirmation of a cautious-neutral stance with management validating margin headwinds at the May-2026 analyst meet. A 'hold what you have, do not add' call.

The analytical value of the Nomura note is precisely that management commentary: if KKC itself guided for persistent margin pressure in FY27E, it is a direct yellow flag for the Jefferies bull case that depends on margin improvement via indigenisation and mix shift. Nomura's caution is the primary stress test I'd apply to any long-side thesis.

IDBI|260529.change: Downgraded Hold→Sell (trendlyne; Nov-2025 Hold PT ₹4,401 → May-2026 Sell PT ₹5,046); no pdfdata match in local library.
IDBI|260529.view:
IDBI is a valuation outlier at Sell with a PT well below even the Kotak Reduce. No report is available in the local library, so the specific reasoning is inaccessible. The PT of ₹5,046 is below the Kotak PT of ₹5,600 and far below the neutral/bull cluster — suggesting a more conservative earnings model or a higher cost of equity assumption rather than a qualitatively distinct fundamental view.

Treat this as the floor of the valuation distribution rather than a high-conviction counter-thesis until the full note becomes available. Worth noting that IDBI raised its PT from ₹4,401 to ₹5,046 even while downgrading — consistent with the pattern of PT upgrades across the board post Q4FY26 results.

Geojit|260507.change: Upgraded to Buy with PT ₹6,160 (May-2026); no prior Geojit entry in library to compare.
Geojit|260507.view: Geojit's Buy is from early May — before the late-May cluster of post-Q4 reports from Jefferies, Kotak, JPMorgan, and Nomura — so the PT of ₹6,160 was likely set on slightly older data. No local report is available. Given the timing, this call may have already been partially superseded by fresher analysis. I would not weight it heavily alongside the more recent notes, though the directional Buy view is in line with Jefferies.

PL|250808.change: Downgraded Buy→Hold (trendlyne; May-2025 Buy PT ₹3,646 → Aug-2025 Hold PT ₹3,895); dated Aug-2025, ~10 months stale.
PL|250808.view: Very stale — PL's Aug-2025 Hold and PT of ₹3,895 pre-dates the DC narrative crystallising and the stock's major re-rating. At a PT that is far below even the current bear case of ₹5,046, this note has no actionable value for current positioning. Discard for investment decision-making until an updated PL note appears.

ICICI|250210.change: Hold with PT ₹2,900 (Feb-2025); no prior ICICI entry to compare. Dated Feb-2025, ~16 months stale.
ICICI|250210.view: Extremely stale and not actionable. ICICI's Feb-2025 Hold at ₹2,900 was written in a completely different valuation context — before CPCB IV+ ramp, before DC emerged as a meaningful revenue segment, and before the stock's substantial re-rating. The PT is far below all other houses and the current market price. Discard entirely for current analysis.

Cyient.summary:
Coverage is split: **JPMorgan** (OW, PT ₹1,100, Jun-2026) and **Geojit** (Buy, PT ₹1,159, Mar-2026) are constructive; **Emkay** (Sell, PT ₹1,150, Oct-2025) and **Kotak** (Reduce, PT ₹880, Jun-2026) are negative; **IDBI** (Hold, PT ₹1,015, Apr-2026) and **ICICI** (Hold, PT ₹1,190, Apr-2025 — stale) sit in the middle. Published targets cluster ₹880–₹1,190. The real fault line is the Tao Digital acquisition (US$218 mn, ~11–12× FY2028E EBITDA): JPMorgan frames it as TAM expansion into data engineering and software product engineering, cross-sell potential, and a shift toward larger annuity deals; Kotak is skeptical, calling it a gap-filler whose value depends entirely on execution. IDBI's sharp downgrade — Buy at ₹1,307 in Jan-2026 → Hold at ₹1,015 by Apr-2026 — reflects earnings disappointment before the deal, and their post-acquisition stance is not yet updated. Emkay's Oct-2025 Sell at ₹1,150 predates the acquisition and is stale on that dimension. Geojit's upgrade to Buy in Mar-2026 looks premature given the deal announcement came later.

My own read: Cyient's core ER&D franchise (aerospace/defence, transportation, communications) is solid but cyclically lumpy and structurally under pressure as clients in-source more digital work. The Tao Digital deal is strategically sensible — DET needed a credible digital/data engineering capability to stay relevant — but US$218 mn at 11–12× forward EBITDA is not a bargain for an asset that still needs to prove cross-sell traction. The bears are right to flag execution risk; the bulls are right that standing still was not an option. At ~₹908 (per JPMorgan's 29-May note), the stock prices in modest execution success, which is a reasonable risk/reward only if integration milestones are on track. I'd watch: (1) deal integration milestones and revenue synergies in H1 FY2027, (2) whether the aerospace/defence pipeline converts (lumpy, but the order book matters a lot), and (3) margin trajectory as Tao's cost base is absorbed. IDBI's downgrade trajectory — from ₹1,307 to ₹1,015 in three months — is the most informative data point in the coverage: it reflects a company that missed near-term expectations hard, not just a re-rating. I'd not chase here without evidence of execution.

IDBI|260424.change: Downgraded from Buy (PT ₹1,307, Jan-2026) to Hold (PT ₹1,015) on 24 Apr 2026 — a sharp cut of ₹292 on the target and a full ratings step-down.
IDBI|260424.view:
This is the most telling move in the coverage set. A Buy-to-Hold downgrade with the target slashed 22% in three months signals that Q3/Q4 results missed IDBI's expectations materially, not just marginally. IDBI was the most bullish house at ₹1,307 and is now the most cautious among non-Sell raters. The downgrade predates the Tao Digital announcement (Jun-2026), so it is a pure earnings call — execution on the core ER&D business is what disappointed.

The current Hold at ₹1,015 means IDBI sees limited near-term upside from ~₹908 CMP. Worth watching whether IDBI updates post-acquisition: if they stay at Hold/₹1,015 despite the deal, that's a meaningful signal that the market is likely already pricing in deal optionality. If they re-initiate higher, the logic would need to rest on cross-sell acceleration — which is hard to verify before FY2027 results.

Geojit|260319.change: Upgraded to Buy (PT ₹1,159) on 19 Mar 2026; no prior Geojit entry in the library to compare.
Geojit|260319.view:
Geojit's Mar-2026 upgrade to Buy at ₹1,159 came before the Tao Digital deal announcement in June. The thesis was presumably a recovery in core ER&D growth after the weak patches in H1 FY2026. At ₹908 CMP, ₹1,159 implies ~28% upside — meaningful, but Geojit is a smaller broker and this upgrade is now five months stale, predating the deal's risk/reward shift.

I'd discount this view somewhat: it doesn't incorporate the acquisition's dilution/leverage effects, and the subsequent IDBI downgrade (a more active tracker) suggests the fundamental picture between Mar and Apr worsened. Geojit has not updated since March, which is a gap.

Emkay|251017.change: Sell rating with PT ₹1,150 as of Oct 2025; no prior Emkay entry to compare. Dated Oct-2025 — over seven months old.
Emkay|251017.view:
Emkay's Oct-2025 Sell at ₹1,150 (headline: 'Steady operating performance; ambitious growth ahead') is a contradiction in terms — a Sell at a target above the then-prevailing price, paired with 'steady' operations and 'ambitious' guidance. This typically signals concern about valuation and execution credibility rather than a fundamental collapse thesis.

The note is now materially stale: it predates the Q3/Q4 disappointment that prompted IDBI's downgrade, and it entirely predates the Tao Digital acquisition. Emkay's current view on the deal is unknown. The Sell label should be interpreted in the Oct-2025 context only — it is not an active, informed bear call on the current situation. I would not rely on this for current positioning.

ICICI|250425.change: Downgraded to Hold (PT ₹1,190) on 25 Apr 2025; no prior ICICI entry to compare. Dated Apr-2025 — over 13 months old, substantially stale.
ICICI|250425.view:
ICICI's Apr-2025 Hold at ₹1,190 is the oldest and most stale note in the set. It predates the significant earnings deterioration (IDBI's downgrade implies Q3/Q4 FY2026 missed hard), and it predates the Tao Digital deal entirely. A Hold at ₹1,190 from over a year ago is not a live view.

The only informational value here is that ICICI was already cautious (downgraded to Hold) even in the relatively benign Apr-2025 environment. If ICICI has not put out a fresh note after the Q4 results or the acquisition, that itself is a signal — they may not have enough conviction to update. I would assign near-zero weight to this for current analysis.

Dalmia Bharat.summary:
Five of six houses are bullish — **CLSA** (Outperform, ₹2,110), **Jefferies** (Buy, ₹2,445), **Nomura** (Buy, ₹2,500), **PL** (Buy, ₹2,287), **MO** (Buy, ₹2,230) — with only **BOB** at Hold (₹2,110), itself an upgrade from Sell after Q4FY26 results (valuation-driven capitulation, not fundamental conversion). Targets cluster ₹2,110–₹2,500; the spread is narrow for a mid-cap cement name. The dominant recent catalyst is the Jaypee Associates acquisition (May 2026): 5.2MT cement + 3.3MT clinker + 99MW thermal power for ₹28.5bn (~USD57/t), reviving a lapsed Dec-22 deal. Jefferies and Nomura both published on the same day — constructive but Jefferies is notably more hedged, flagging old assets, refurbishment needs, and sharpened Central India competition. The real fault line is not the rating (consensus is long) but the **volume recovery thesis**: MO cut its PT ~13% from ₹2,570 to ₹2,230 in two months (Feb–Apr 2026) while keeping Buy, and PL's Q4FY26 note names volume recovery as still-pending "the key" catalyst. The Q4FY26 earnings beat was cost-led, not volume-led — important context.

My own read: Dalmia has historically been the most disciplined capital allocator among mid-cap Indian cement names — its East+South coastal footprint provides freight cost advantages and structural insulation from the most competitive pockets. The Jaypee acquisition is strategically sound (geographic diversification, re-entry to Central India) but execution risk is material: old, refurbishment-requiring assets in a region where **Adani**, **UltraTech**, and **Shree** compete hard. The ₹28.5bn price is cheap in absolute EV/t terms, but cheap assets in a tough market need management execution, not just a favourable entry price. The management message on no equity raise and leverage below 1.4x (CLSA meeting note, Jun 2026) is reassuring if it holds; MO's quiet TP cut is the counterweight, signalling near-term earnings power is settling lower. I'd sit at the lower end of the bull camp — constructive on franchise quality but not ahead of volume recovery proving itself. Two things to watch: (1) Q1–Q2 FY27 volumes — if the recovery materialises, the cost discipline already embedded makes earnings upside sharp; (2) JPA asset ramp-up capex and EBITDA/t progress toward CLSA's implied ₹1,000/t target by FY29.

CLSA|260604.change: PT ₹2,110 unchanged; Outperform maintained (pdfdata: prevTP ₹2,110 = currTP ₹2,110, prevCall OP = currCall OP). Meeting-takeaway note — no rating event.
CLSA|260604.view:
CLSA's Jun 2026 meeting note captures two key management assurances: no equity dilution, and net leverage below 1.4x post the Jaypee acquisition. These are precisely the pain points bears would press, so CLSA is delivering a 'management says the obvious concerns are managed' note rather than fresh analysis.

The OP with a ₹2,110 PT is the most conservative target in the bull camp (tied with BOB's Hold), which is telling — CLSA is constructive but apparently pricing in limited near-term upside, likely building in a slow JPA ramp-up. The 'no equity raise' commitment is worth monitoring over the next two quarters as refurbishment capex on the acquired assets starts to flow through.

Jeff|260522.change: PT ₹2,445; Buy maintained. First report captured in library for this acquisition note (prevTP null in pdfdata); prevCall noted as BUY, suggesting rating continuity, but no prior PT is available to measure the change.
Jeff|260522.view:
Jefferies frames the Jaypee deal as 'Enters Central Region Again' — deliberately echoing the lapsed Dec-22 attempt, signalling this is a second bite at the same strategic goal. Their ~USD70/t figure (vs Nomura's USD57/t on cement/clinker alone) likely includes attributed value for the 99MW thermal power and railway sidings, making the two houses roughly consistent on deal economics.

The note is constructively cautious: Jefferies acknowledges the assets are old, require refurbishment, and will intensify Central India competition — but backs the deal on the logic that Adani's divestiture was balance-sheet driven (distress seller) and Dalmia has prior regional familiarity. At ₹2,445 they sit mid-range among bulls. The risks Jeff quietly flags — old assets, tough competitive dynamics — are exactly the execution variables I'd stress-test over the next 12 months.

Nomura|260522.change: PT ₹2,500 unchanged; Buy maintained (pdfdata: prevTP ₹2,500 = currTP ₹2,500, prevCall BUY = currCall BUY). Same-day note as Jefferies on the Jaypee acquisition.
Nomura|260522.view:
Nomura holds the highest PT in the set at ₹2,500 and their note is notably precise on deal terms: 5.2MT cement + 3.3MT clinker + 99MW thermal + railway sidings for ₹28.5bn. The attention to the power and logistics assets — which other houses treat as a footnote — matters for the long-run operating cost structure once integrated.

The unchanged ₹2,500 PT through the acquisition announcement reads as 'the deal is roughly NPV-neutral at this price' — Nomura either had this deal probability partly baked in or sees the incremental value as modest. At ₹2,500, they are the most optimistic house; I'd want to understand what volume and EBITDA/t assumptions underpin that number, given how far MO has moved its estimates down in the same period.

BOB|260429.change: Upgraded from Sell to Hold; PT raised ₹2,087→₹2,110 (trendlyne history: 251017 Sell ₹2,087 → 260429 Hold ₹2,110).
BOB|260429.view:
BOB was the persistent bear — Sell at ₹1,926 (Jul 2025), Sell at ₹2,087 (Oct 2025) — and has now moved to a grudging Hold after Q4FY26 results. The upgrade language ('valuations reasonable') is classic valuation-driven capitulation: they've stopped fighting the stock, but they haven't turned constructive on the business.

A PT of ₹2,110 (lowest in the set, tied with CLSA's Outperform) signals BOB sees minimal upside even from Hold. The 'long-term challenges' language from their Oct 2025 Sell note presumably still underpins the view — Q4FY26 wasn't enough to change that narrative, only to close the valuation gap. I'd read BOB as the useful contrarian anchor: the bear case (competitive pressures, structural volume growth challenges) isn't dead, it's just currently losing the argument on valuation.

PL|260429.change: First PL entry in trendlyne coverage; no prior to compare. PT ₹2,287; Buy.
PL|260429.view:
PL's headline — 'cost-led beat; volume recovery remains the key' — is the most candid framing in the bull camp. A cost-led beat means margins surprised on input cost tailwinds or opex discipline, not on pricing power or volume leverage. That's a decent quarter, but not the earnings quality that justifies re-rating higher.

PL's explicit flag that volume recovery 'remains the key' is an admission that the bull thesis is still conditional on demand delivery. Their ₹2,287 PT sits mid-range among the bulls; Buy is credible given the franchise quality, but this note reads more like 'constructive, waiting for the demand inflection' than high-conviction Buy. I agree with their framing — volume delivery in the next two quarters is the pivot point for this stock.

MO|260428.change: PT lowered ₹2,570→₹2,230; Buy maintained (trendlyne: 260212 Buy ₹2,570 → 260428 Buy ₹2,230 — a ~13% cut in approximately two months).
MO|260428.view:
MO's ~13% PT cut while keeping Buy is the most informative data point in this set. When a house cuts its target 13% in two months without changing the rating, it is signalling that near-term earnings estimates have come down materially but the analyst is unwilling to admit a rating error. The note headline — 'muted volume growth; lower opex/t drive profitability' — confirms what PL also flagged: Q4FY26 was a cost beat, not a volume beat.

MO had held ₹2,570 through Jan–Feb 2026; the step-down to ₹2,230 is where post-Q4 consensus earnings appear to be settling. I'd take MO's revised ₹2,230 as the most honest near-term fair value anchor in the set — it prices in the volume underwhelm and modest earnings quality without abandoning the medium-term capacity story. Their earlier ₹2,570 now looks like it was pricing in a volume recovery that has not arrived.

Deepak Nitrite.summary:
**Kotak** (May-2026, ADD, PT ₹1,950) is the lone active bull, writing up 4QFY26 windfall from Iran-war-driven phenol-spread spike; they raised FY27E EPS 55% and rolled their fair value to ₹1,950. **PL** (Apr-2026, Reduce, PT ₹1,354) downgraded sharply, flagging structural margin risk from polycarbonate capacity additions. **MO** (Aug-2025, Sell, PT ₹1,630) and **ICICI** (Aug-2025, Hold, PT ₹1,950) are both over nine months stale and predate the Iran-war windfall entirely. The PT spread is wide — ₹1,354 to ₹1,950 — with the entire gap reflecting disagreement on whether phenolics margins have a durable floor. The real fault line is whether the Iran-war phenol spike marks a cyclical reset higher or is a one-off windfall that fades, leaving Deepak exposed to global polycarbonate overcapacity.

My own read: Deepak Nitrite's earnings are dominated by Deepak Phenolics' phenol–BPA–acetone spread dynamics, which are among the most volatile in Indian specialty chemicals. Kotak's near-term upgrade is arithmetically correct given 4QFY26 outperformance, but the report itself flags that spreads have already corrected sharply post-quarter — the FY28E EPS was only lifted 8% versus 55% for FY27E, a clear tell that even the bull house doesn't believe the windfall is durable. PL's polycarbonate capacity-addition concern is the more enduring structural risk: new domestic and Asian PC capacity has historically compressed margins for integrated phenol players and this dynamic is slow-moving and does not reverse on a single geopolitical episode. On balance I'd treat this as a show-me story over 12–18 months: if phenol spreads stabilise above the FY25 trough on sustained supply disruption, Kotak's ADD works; if they mean-revert (the historical base case once disruptions ease), FY27E estimates face cuts and PL's ₹1,354 becomes more defensible. The two things I'd watch most: monthly phenol–cumene spread data and the commissioning timeline of new polycarbonate capacity (domestic or Chinese export pressure).

Kotak|260518.change: PT raised ₹1,810→₹1,950; ADD maintained. FY2027E EPS upgraded 55% on phenol windfall; FY2028E up only 8%. FV rolled to Jun-2027.
Kotak|260518.view:
Kotak's ADD is defensible in the narrow context of 4QFY26 earnings — the Iran-war spike in phenol spreads was a genuine, if transient, boost and the 55% near-term EPS upgrade reflects real outperformance. But the asymmetry between the FY27E upgrade (55%) and FY28E (8%) is the most important line in the report: Kotak is implicitly embedding mean-reversion, which means the ADD is a 1-year trade, not a structural re-rating.

The key risk is that spreads were already correcting 'sharply in recent weeks' per Kotak's own note at the time of writing. If the correction deepened through May–June 2026, FY27E estimates may themselves need a trim before year-end. At ₹1,950 ADD the risk/reward for fresh buyers is narrow unless phenol spreads find a higher floor than pre-war levels — a geopolitical assumption that deserves stress-testing.

PL|260413.change: Downgraded from Hold (PT ₹1,673, Feb-2026) to Reduce (PT ₹1,354, Apr-2026); PT cut ~19%.
PL|260413.view:
PL's downgrade is the most substantive structural bear call in the set and the one I'd take most seriously on a 12–18 month view. Polycarbonate capacity additions — domestic and from Asian exporters — threaten BPA margins at Deepak Phenolics, the primary earnings engine. A ₹1,354 PT implies material downside from current levels and reflects a view that the phenolics cycle has peaked structurally, not just cyclically.

The capacity-addition dynamic PL flags is slow-moving and persistent — it does not reverse with a geopolitical spread spike. If PL is right, the Iran-war windfall merely delayed the reckoning by a quarter or two. I'd watch GAIL's domestic polycarbonate commissioning timeline and Chinese BPA export-price trends as the key falsifying data for this thesis; if either shows signs of pressure, PL's call will look prescient even against Kotak's near-term optimism.

MO|250815.change: Dated Aug-2025; no prior MO report in the library to compare. Sell, PT ₹1,630.
MO|250815.view:
This note is over nine months old, predates both the 4QFY26 windfall and PL's polycarbonate downgrade, and should be treated as historical background rather than an active live call. MO's Sell with ₹1,630 PT likely reflected the persistent margin compression through FY25–Q1FY26. The stock has almost certainly repriced significantly above MO's PT after the Iran-war windfall quarter.

Until MO publishes an updated note, their directional stance (Sell) is consistent with the structural bear camp but the specific TP is not actionable. The absence of an update since Aug-2025 is itself a data point — a broker that strongly disagrees with a windfall re-rating usually publishes quickly.

ICICI|250815.change: Hold maintained vs prior Hold (PT ₹2,000, May-2025); PT trimmed ₹2,000→₹1,950. New capex commissioning flagged as H2FY26 earnings catalyst.
ICICI|250815.view:
ICICI's Aug-2025 Hold was the most balanced view at the time — cautious on near-term margins but constructive on the capex commissioning cycle providing a recovery path. The PT was only marginally trimmed (₹2,000→₹1,950), signalling cautious optimism rather than a structural bear stance.

Like MO, this note is over nine months stale and its specific catalyst (new capex commissioning aiding H2FY26 growth) has since been superseded by the Iran-war windfall dynamic. An updated ICICI note would be valuable: did the windfall push them toward ADD (joining Kotak), or did polycarbonate capacity risk push them toward Reduce (joining PL)? The stale Hold is not informative for current positioning and should be weighted accordingly.

Divi's Laboratories.summary:
Eight houses cover Divi's, split four-bull / two-neutral / two-bear. **JPMorgan** (OW, ₹7,400), **Jefferies** (Buy, ₹7,950), **PL** (Accumulate, ₹6,900), and **DC** (Accumulate, ₹6,795) form the constructive camp; **Kotak** (Sell, ₹5,850) is the most pointed fresh bear; **ICICI** (Sell, ₹5,400) maintains its Sell but that note is from Nov-2025 and predates Q4FY26 results entirely. **BOB** (Hold, ₹7,500 — paradoxically the highest Hold target in the set) and **Geojit** (Hold, ₹6,336, upgraded from Sell in Apr-2026) occupy the middle. The fresh-target spread runs ₹5,850 (Kotak) to ₹7,950 (Jefferies) against a late-May CMP of ~₹6,887. Q4FY26 was universally soft — EBITDA missed estimates by ~24% — yet the bulls shrugged it off, pointing to management's double-digit FY27 guidance and the peptide CDMO pipeline. **Jefferies** trimmed its target modestly (₹8,100→₹7,950) but held Buy; **JPMorgan** nudged it up (₹7,300→₹7,400), staying OW. **Kotak**'s Sell is the credible counterweight: it flags that Divi's must rapidly replace Entresto EU contract revenue as the molecule ages, and that commercialisation of the next CS wave remains unproven.

My own read: Divi's is the highest-quality CDMO franchise in India — pristine balance sheet, zero debt, a regulatory track record built over decades, and the deep client stickiness that matters for complex custom synthesis. But the bull case requires faith in a pipeline that has been 'upcoming' for several quarters now. The issue the sell-side dances around is Entresto dependency: sacubitril/valsartan is among Divi's largest CS molecules, and as the branded product matures in Western markets, contract volumes face a real ceiling — Kotak is right to flag this as a monitorable. Management's peptide ambitions are real (capex is committed, first-mover advantage among Indian CDMOs), but the gap between 'development stage projects' and meaningful P&L contribution is likely 18–24 months. The Q4FY26 EBITDA miss was a yellow flag, not just noise — it reflects pricing pressure and a product mix that is still in transition. I'd sit closer to BOB's cautious Hold than Jefferies' conviction Buy at current levels: the franchise deserves a premium, but that premium already prices in a smoother CS-to-peptide handoff than the evidence supports. Watch: (1) any Q1FY27 guidance on Entresto EU volumes; (2) first meaningful peptide CS revenue line, even a small one — that de-risks the timeline narrative considerably.

PL|260525.change: PT raised ₹6,550→₹6,900 vs prior Aug-2025 note (per trendlyne); Accumulate maintained.
PL|260525.view: PL's Accumulate is a qualified positive — the 'EBITDA miss; Peptide opportunities key for growth' headline captures the tension well. The ₹6,900 target is conservative relative to the bull camp, implying PL sees the peptide upside as real but still years from meaningful P&L contribution. The measured sequential PT lift from ₹6,550 is neither enthusiastic nor dismissive. This reads as a sensible hold-your-horses call: comfortable holding, not excited to add aggressively until CS project timelines firm up post-regulatory approvals. Fresh (May-2026) and honest about the near-term miss — one of the more balanced takes in the set.

JP|260524.view:
JPMorgan's OW is the most institutionally-credible bull call here. The marginal ₹100 raise is honest — it is not momentum-chasing after a tepid Q4, just a small mark-to-market on the target. JPMorgan correctly identifies currency (INR depreciation benefits export revenues) as a partial tailwind and flags Middle East freight disruption as a cost headwind that management expects to be partly offset.

The note's emphasis on 'peptide ambitions building, custom synthesis commercialisation to unlock next leg of growth' is the thesis, not yet the evidence. The ₹7,400 target needs double-digit FY27 guidance to materialise as actual revenue; any guidance cut mid-year would put the OW under pressure. Still, among the bulls, JPMorgan's framing is the most grounded in what the numbers actually showed.

Kotak|260524.change: No prior captured in the library for Kotak on this company (prevTP null in pdfdata); SELL maintained. PT ₹5,850 disclosed in this note.
Kotak|260524.view:
Kotak's Sell at ₹5,850 — roughly 15% below late-May CMP — is the most analytically specific bear thesis in the coverage. The 'The wait continues' title is pointed: the market has been waiting for CS commercialisation for several quarters, and Kotak argues the wait will extend further. The Entresto angle is the key one: as Novartis navigates biosimilar and genericisation pressure in Europe, Divi's CS volumes from this molecule face a real ceiling, and the speed with which Divi's can replace that revenue with newer commercial molecules is the unproven assumption the bulls are making.

I'd stress-test ₹5,850 against the other side: that target likely embeds both a generic API recovery stall and a delayed CS transition. It may underweight the franchise floor (zero-debt CDMO with global client relationships) and the option value of the peptide infrastructure Divi's is already building. Not a screaming Buy at current levels, but Kotak's ₹5,850 feels too punitive if even one large peptide CS contract announces in FY27. Use this call as the bear case, not the base.

BOB|260524.change: PT raised ₹6,851→₹7,500 vs prior Aug-2025 note (per trendlyne); Hold maintained.
BOB|260524.view: BOB's Hold hides a surprisingly bullish ₹7,500 target — actually higher than JPMorgan's OW price target — which makes the Hold rating a curious choice. The 'margin headwinds to persist near-term' framing explains the rating; BOB is saying short-term pain is likely even though the medium-term target is constructive. The ~9% PT raise from ₹6,851 is meaningful and suggests BOB has grown more positive on the terminal story even if it is cautious about quarterly execution. The prior note's emphasis on 'long-term supply agreements' as a moat is worth noting — these locked-in CS commitments provide revenue visibility the bears tend to underweight. At ₹7,500 this is almost a stealth OW; the Hold label is doing a lot of near-term hedging work.

Jeff|260523.view:
Jefferies has the highest target in the coverage at ₹7,950 (~15% above May CMP) and is the conviction bull. The modest cut reflects the Q4 miss and delayed CS project timelines — not a change in structural thesis. Jefferies is specifically highlighting 17% YoY CS/nutraceutical growth and Divi's stated ambition to become a large-scale peptide manufacturer as the reasons to stay constructive.

The credibility test: Jefferies explicitly acknowledges 'timelines for key CS projects remain unclear due to regulatory approvals' and still rates it Buy. That is an unusual admission — it tells you the call is event-dependent, not already in the earnings run-rate. Treat ₹7,950 as an upside scenario target (smooth project commercialisation in FY27), not a conservative base. Jefferies would be right if the peptide timeline de-risks; they would look early if it drags into FY28.

Geojit|260406.change: Upgraded to Hold from Sell; PT raised ₹5,400→₹6,336 vs prior Sep-2025 Sell note (per trendlyne).
Geojit|260406.view: Geojit's upgrade from Sell to Hold in Apr-2026 was directionally right — the stock had materially re-rated since the Sep-2025 Sell at ₹5,400. At ₹6,336, however, the Hold target now sits below late-May CMP (~₹6,887), making this note already stale on its own terms — Geojit would technically need to issue a fresh note to justify Hold vs Reduce at current prices. Low weight to this call given the vintage and the below-CMP target.

DC|251120.change: PT raised ₹6,499→₹6,795 vs prior Aug-2025 note (per trendlyne); Accumulate maintained.
DC|251120.view: The Deven Choksey note is from Nov-2025 — now over 6 months old — and predates Q4FY26 results entirely. The ₹6,795 target is also below late-May CMP (~₹6,887), making the Accumulate call technically stale in both time and price. The observation that 'CS traction and favorable mix boosted profitability' was accurate for Q2FY26 but Q4FY26 told a different story. Minimal weight until DC refreshes post-Q4.

ICICI|251109.change: PT raised ₹3,670→₹5,400 vs prior Aug-2024 note (per trendlyne); Sell maintained.
ICICI|251109.view: The ICICI Sell from Nov-2025 is the stalest substantive view in the coverage — now 7 months old, predating Q4FY26 results. The ₹5,400 target sits ~21% below late-May CMP, making it the most bearish in the set. The thesis ('generics continue to drag; CS outlook unchanged') was reasonable at the time but Q4FY26 actually showed CS/nutraceuticals growing 17% YoY — the CS picture has shifted even if EBITDA missed. Discount this call heavily until ICICI publishes a post-Q4 update.

EPL.summary:
All three covered houses are bullish with Buy ratings, but targets diverge meaningfully: **ICICI** ₹315, **Nomura** ₹300, **MO** ₹270 — a 17% spread from top to bottom. The unifying thesis is the Indovida merger (CCI-approved, expected to close by 4QFY27) that repositions EPL from a laminated-tube specialist into a multi-platform emerging-markets packaging company. **Nomura**'s May 2026 management meeting note is the most current and focused squarely on merger mechanics, maintaining its ₹300 target unchanged. **ICICI** raised its target from ₹275 to ₹315 in March 2026, reflecting the most constructive read on EPL's multi-geography expansion story. **MO** has the most instructive recent history — steadily cutting its PT from ₹315 (Nov 2024) to ₹260 (Nov 2025) as organic performance disappointed, before a modest recovery to ₹270 in March 2026. The real debate sits between MO's more grounded ₹270 and ICICI's optimistic ₹315: how much value should the market ascribe to the Indovida integration before it closes and demonstrates synergies?

My own read: EPL is a steady but narrow-moat business — laminated tubes are relatively commoditized, and its durable advantages rest on long-term FMCG relationships (Colgate, Unilever, etc.) and sustainability/innovation capabilities rather than pricing power. The Indovida deal is strategically sensible but introduces real execution risk: Indovida is unlisted with limited public financial disclosure, making integration uncertainty hard to model. MO's ₹270 looks more defensible near-term — the India segment has disappointed on margins for several quarters, and paying a merger-story premium before the deal closes is a leap. I'd watch: (1) India segment EBITDA margin trajectory over the next two quarters, and (2) any incremental disclosure on Indovida's revenue and margin profile at or before deal close. ICICI's ₹315 is achievable only if organic recovery and merger synergies deliver simultaneously — the bull case, not the base.

Nomura|260529.change: PT unchanged at ₹300; Buy maintained. pdfdata confirms prevTP ₹300 → currTP ₹300, prevCall BUY → currCall BUY.
Nomura|260529.view:
Nomura's note is a management meeting takeaway dated May 2026 — the most current view in the library. The substance is entirely focused on the Indovida merger: CCI approval secured, deal expected to close by 4QFY27. Crucially, Nomura did not raise its target on this news, which is telling — at ₹300 it sees fair value but is not chasing merger optionality aggressively.

This measured stance makes Nomura the most credible near-term read: they had recent management access, heard the merger update directly, and kept the target flat. That implies they are not yet extrapolating synergies that haven't been quantified. The note's practical value is confirmation that the merger timeline is on track; it is not itself a re-rating catalyst.

ICICI|260331.change: PT raised ₹275→₹315 (prior Trendlyne entry Aug 2024); Buy maintained throughout. No pdfdata match — sourced from Trendlyne. Note: ~19-month gap between captured entries.
ICICI|260331.view:
ICICI is the most constructive house, framing EPL as 'transitioning to multi-platform packaging with wider geographical reach' — language that maps directly to the Indovida merger logic. The PT raise from ₹275 to ₹315 is sizable, though the 19-month gap between Trendlyne entries makes it difficult to pinpoint the precise trigger.

I'd treat ICICI's ₹315 as an aspirational scenario price rather than a near-term anchor. It bakes in execution that hasn't occurred yet — the merger hasn't closed, Indovida's financials are not public, and EPL's organic India margins have been soft. Useful as the bull-case marker, but I'd want to see a quarter or two of post-merger results before underwriting this target.

MO|260330.change: PT raised ₹260→₹270 (prior Trendlyne entry Nov 2025, TP ₹260, Buy); Buy maintained. Context: this small uptick follows a sustained cutting cycle — TP was ₹315 (Nov 2024), cut to ₹300 (Feb 2025), ₹280 (Aug 2025), ₹260 (Nov 2025), before recovering to ₹270 in Mar 2026.
MO|260330.view:
MO's EPL history is the most instructive: four consecutive PT cuts from ₹315 to ₹260 as organic results — particularly Americas and Europe margins — came in below earlier estimates, before a modest ₹270 uptick in March 2026 as the merger thesis took hold. The 'building a scaled consumer packaging leader for emerging markets' framing signals MO is now leaning into the new story rather than defending the old one.

The small ₹260→₹270 raise is meaningful as a directional inflection but the level itself is sober — at ₹270 MO prices EPL well below both Nomura (₹300) and ICICI (₹315). I find this the most credible valuation anchor: it reflects organic disappointments already embedded and gives limited credit for synergies yet to materialise. The trigger for MO to move meaningfully higher would be India segment margins recovering and the merger closing on schedule without dilutive surprises.

Eicher Motors.summary:
Eight houses cover Eicher Motors with a wide ₹2,300 price-target spread (₹6,500–₹8,800). **Jefferies** is the most bullish (Buy/₹8,800, 15% EPS CAGR FY26–28), followed by **JPMorgan** (OW/₹7,700), **CLSA** (OP/₹7,651), and **Prabhudas Lilladhar** (Accumulate/₹7,580). **BOB Capital** and **Motilal Oswal** sit neutral (Hold/₹7,431 and Neutral/₹6,960 respectively). **Bernstein** is cautiously negative (MP/₹7,000), asking whether momentum has peaked. **Kotak** is the lone clear bear (Sell/₹6,500) — the only house arguing that profitability pressure will structurally weigh on the stock. Post Q4FY26 results (a modest beat on EBITDA), CLSA raised its PT ₹7,454→₹7,651 while JPMorgan nudged its PT slightly lower ₹7,760→₹7,700; Jefferies and Kotak both held unchanged. The real debate is not volume — Royal Enfield grew 23% domestically in FY26 with April 2026 tracking +37% — but whether commodity inflation (~3.5% headwind in 1QFY27, partially offset by ~240bps of cumulative price hikes) and the cost of sustaining volume momentum will compress EBITDA margins below the 24–25% band as capacity expands toward 2M units by FY28.

My own read: Royal Enfield is one of the more defensible consumer franchises in Indian two-wheelers — a category creator with genuine pricing power that Bajaj (Triumph tie-up) and Hero (Harley) have not yet successfully challenged at scale. But the stock is priced for compounding, and the margin-vs-volume tension Kotak flags is legitimate: RE has historically used brand to sustain premium margins, and if the competitive response forces it into a volume-at-cost strategy, the valuation case frays quickly. Bernstein's "has momentum peaked?" is the right question for a disciplined buyer. I'd lean constructive — closer to CLSA/JPM than Kotak or Bernstein — but with two firm watchpoints: (1) whether 1QFY27 EBITDA margins hold above 24% after the full commodity hit lands; and (2) international revenue traction, which remains small but is the long-run bull case's most underdiscussed variable.

JP|260525.view: JPMorgan's OW is credible — the less-than-1% PT trim reflects modest margin conservatism post-Q4, not a fundamental rethink. The "jostling between growth and margins" framing is the right analytical lens: JPM is saying RE's volume story is intact but margin pressure is real and will persist into 1QFY27. I'd agree with the OW directionally, with the key test being whether April's 170bps price hike is sufficient to offset the 3.5% commodity headwind in the next quarterly print.

BOB|260525.change: TP raised ₹6,931→₹7,431 (vs. Feb 2026 report); Hold maintained.
BOB|260525.view: BOB has maintained a neutral stance across multiple Eicher result cycles — the 7% PT raise here is an upward revision but the Hold retention signals they see the stock as fairly valued at current prices. "Priced-in valuations" is defensible when the near-term catalysts (capacity ramp, new launches) are well-telegraphed and the stock has re-rated already. Not a useful input for inflection calls but a reasonable valuation sanity-check on the range.

CLSA|260523.view: CLSA provides the most granular commodity analysis in this set: ~90bps headwind in Q4, ~3.5% in 1QFY27, offset by ~240bps of cumulative price hikes plus cost optimisation and operating leverage. Their "No surprises" framing and maintained OP after an in-line quarter is a steady constructive signal. I'd use CLSA's margin decomposition as the best available modelling input; the management confidence in "offsetting the bulk" of commodity drag deserves a small haircut — RE has historically been optimistic on margin recovery timelines.

Kotak|260523.view: Kotak sits ₹1,000–₹2,300 below every other PT in the pack and has maintained Sell across at least two result cycles. Their structural case — RE is sacrificing profitability for volume share, leaving margins under sustained pressure — has internal consistency but the data doesn't yet confirm a structural break: 21% YoY EBITDA growth and 24.9% margins in Q4 are not the profile of a company losing pricing power. Kotak is right that margin vs volume is the tension to watch, but Sell requires a more severe outcome than current trends imply. Most useful as a bear stress-test: model EBITDA margins settling at 22% vs the consensus 24–25% and see where the stock lands.

PL|260523.change: Trendlyne shows TP ₹7,580, Accumulate (May 2026); no earlier PL report in the library to compare against.
PL|260523.view: PL's Accumulate aligns with the constructive consensus post an in-line Q4. Limited paragraph detail is available (trendlyne-sourced only), so there is little analytical differentiation to assess. Directionally consistent with CLSA/JPM but without the granularity to weight independently.

Bern|260522.change: First captured Bernstein report for Eicher; PT ₹7,000, Market Perform; no prior Bernstein report in library to compare.
Bern|260522.view: Bernstein's "has momentum peaked?" is the most intellectually substantive bear contribution in this set — rather than arguing the near-term numbers are wrong, they question the durability of RE's competitive moat as the segment it created attracts well-resourced entrants. MP/₹7,000 is cautious but not a Sell; they see limited upside rather than downside risk. This is a useful framing for a disciplined investor: not "RE is broken" but "RE is at fair value and risk/reward is unfavourable vs. consensus bulls." The empirical test is relative market share in the 350–450cc band over the next 4 quarters — if RE holds 80%+ share through the competitive response, the Bernstein case weakens materially.

Jeff|260522.view: Jefferies is the most bullish house, assigning a premium multiple to RE's franchise quality and global optionality. Their 15% EPS CAGR for FY26–28 and assertion that "the toughest phase of competition is behind" is the most conviction-heavy call in the pack — and the direct counterpoint to Bernstein. I'd take the bullish direction but apply a modest discount to the ₹8,800 PT: it requires both margin recovery and volume compounding simultaneously, which is a tighter path than the current commodity environment allows. If margins compress to 23% on the 1QFY27 cycle, the PT needs to step down.

MO|260327.change: Trendlyne shows upgrade to Neutral, TP ₹6,960 (Mar 2026); no prior Motilal entry in library to confirm the prior rating.
MO|260327.view: Motilal's Mar 2026 note is now two months stale and predates Q4 results that came in modestly ahead of consensus. At ₹6,960 their PT is the second-lowest among covering houses. The upgrade to Neutral suggests prior caution, but without a post-Q4 update this note carries low current weight. Worth tracking for a refresh — if Motilal upgrades again post-Q4 it would be a meaningful signal given their typically well-modelled India auto coverage.

Emami.summary:
Seven houses cover Emami but the views are sharply bifurcated by vintage. The two fresh post-Q4FY26 notes (Jefferies, CLSA) tell a sober story: revenues fell 4% YoY, the summer portfolio cratered 22% YoY (Middle East war + seasonal disruption), EBITDA missed consensus by ~16%, and both houses cut their targets. **Jefferies** holds at Buy (₹620) but candidly says the call is "based solely on valuations" — not conviction. **CLSA** is the lone Hold (₹415), the lowest target in the pack and ~49% below Jefferies, underlining an unusually wide disagreement for a ₹17,000 Cr market-cap consumer name. **KS** (Buy, ₹525, May-2026) similarly trimmed its target from ₹589 while expecting a 1H FY27 recovery. The Feb-2026 vintage (**MO** Buy ₹650, **PL** Accumulate ₹571) pre-dates the Q4 miss and overstates the near-term picture; the Nov-2024 notes from **Emkay** (Buy ₹950) and **AR** (Buy ₹900) are stale by over 18 months. The real debate is between CLSA's operating-deleverage/structural-concern stance and Jefferies' valuation-floor argument — and the ₹415 vs ₹620 gap is telling.

My own read: Emami is a genuinely niche franchise — Navratna, BoroPlus, Zandu, Smart & Handsome — but Jefferies' own admission that EBITDA has been flat for five years is the most important data point in this coverage universe. This is not a cyclical wobble; it is a business that has serially disappointed. The structural issues are real: heavy summer/seasonal skew makes revenues lumpy and weather-sensitive; the Middle East (healthcare/BoT export segment) is a geopolitical hostage; and the mass-personal-care space faces intensifying competition from D2C brands and HUL. The valuation case (Jefferies) depends on mean-reversion to historical multiples — plausible if the cycle turns, dangerous if it doesn't. I'd want to see two consecutive quarters of summer-portfolio volume recovery before accepting the thesis. CLSA's Hold is the more intellectually honest stance right now. Key things to watch: Q1 FY27 summer-portfolio YoY (did the Middle East disruption ease and did weather cooperate?), gross-margin trajectory (the 255bps YoY improvement is encouraging and needs to persist), and any signal on the Zandu/wellness segment filling the EBITDA gap.

KS|260526.change: PT cut ₹589→₹525 (prior Trendlyne entry Feb-2026); Buy maintained.
KS|260526.view:
KS is the only house with a fresh May-2026 note that still rates Emami a Buy, though the target trim to ₹525 from ₹589 reflects reduced near-term confidence. The framing — geopolitical headwinds (Middle East) plus seasonal drag — is consistent with the Q4 data, and the 1H FY27 recovery thesis (normalising Middle East, summer portfolio lapping a weak base) is plausible.

However, KS's own target trajectory tells a clear story: ₹944 (Nov-2024) → ₹645 (Nov-2025) → ₹589 (Feb-2026) → ₹525 (May-2026). That is a consistent downgrade trend across every earnings season, suggesting the recovery keeps slipping one quarter forward. I'd treat the Buy as a valuation-floor argument rather than a growth conviction, and wait for Q1 FY27 data before acting on it.

CLSA|260522.change: No prior CLSA report in the library to compare; Hold initiated at ₹415.
CLSA|260522.view:
CLSA's note is the most bearish in the current pack and the most analytically granular: it pins the EBITDA miss at 16% vs consensus, breaks out gross-margin improvement (255bps YoY — a genuine positive) against EBITDA-margin compression (260bps YoY from operating deleverage and higher A&P), and calls out the summer-portfolio collapse as the decisive drag. At ₹415, CLSA is pricing in very little near-term recovery.

This is the useful counterweight to the consensus-bull stance. The operating-deleverage argument is sound: if revenue grows only weakly or declines, Emami's cost base doesn't flex proportionally, and A&P spending to defend shelf space compounds the margin pressure. I think CLSA's structural concerns are underweighted by the bull houses. ₹415 may be closer to fair value if the growth recovery is another two or three quarters away.

Jeff|260521.view:
Jefferies is technically the most bullish (highest PT at ₹620) but its own language reveals a reluctant bull — the BUY is explicitly "based solely on valuations", not earnings confidence. When an analyst flags that, it is a yellow flag: valuation support works until sentiment turns further negative, and Emami has a history of re-ratings going in the wrong direction.

The flat-EBITDA-for-five-years admission is the most important line in any recent Emami note. Jefferies is essentially arguing: yes, this business hasn't grown earnings in half a decade, but the stock is cheap enough on mean-reversion. That is a reasonable argument in theory, but mean-reversion requires a catalyst — and the Q4 miss doesn't supply one. I'd discount the ₹620 target and focus on whether Q1 FY27 data validates the recovery narrative before treating this as a conviction buy.

MO|260204.change: PT cut ₹675→₹650 (prior Trendlyne entry Nov-2025); Buy maintained.
MO|260204.view:
This is a pre-Q4FY26 note based on Q3FY26 results. MO was cautiously optimistic — steady delivery, positive commentary on growth recovery — but the subsequent Q4 miss makes this view stale. The ₹650 target now sits above even Jefferies' post-miss ₹620, making MO the most optimistic in the current set on an apples-to-apples basis.

MO's view needs to be refreshed post-Q4. The Q3 beat that underpinned this note was followed by a Q4 that missed EBITDA by ~16%. The recovery story MO was banking on did not materialise in Q4. Treat this as an old data point until a post-results update appears.

PL|260204.change: PT cut ₹697→₹571 (prior Trendlyne entry May-2025); Accumulate maintained.
PL|260204.view:
PL's Accumulate from February 2026 is similarly pre-Q4 and based on Q3FY26 results. At ₹571 it is more conservative than MO and Jefferies, and PL's "cautiously optimistic" framing was an honest hedge at the time. PL has historically been more measured on Emami than the bull pack.

Like MO, this view is now stale post-Q4. PL's Accumulate (rather than Buy) has arguably been the more defensible stance given the serial earnings misses. The ₹571 target will likely be revised down once PL refreshes its note for Q4FY26.

Emkay|241110.change: Dated Nov-2024 (over 18 months old); no recent prior to compare.
Emkay|241110.view:
Emkay's Buy at ₹950 from November 2024 is deeply stale — the stock has derated materially since and the company has missed estimates in multiple quarters since that note was written. "Better seasonality and focus on execution" was the thesis in Q2FY25; Emami has delivered neither consistently in the 18 months since.

Disregard this note for current investment decisions. Emkay almost certainly has a refreshed, lower target, but it is not in the library.

AR|241110.change: Dated Nov-2024 (over 18 months old); no recent prior to compare.
AR|241110.view:
Anand Rathi's Buy at ₹900 from November 2024 carries the same staleness problem as Emkay. The TMC trade-channel transition and Bangladesh headwinds AR flagged in Q2FY25 have been followed by further disappointments — the H2 FY25 recovery AR was expecting has not fully played through.

The ₹900 target is not a usable data point in the current context.

Entero Healthcare.summary:
Only **Jefferies** (May 2026) and **Monarch** (Aug 2024) cover Entero in the library — both bullish, no bears. Jefferies is the only current, substantive view: it raised its PT from ₹1,350 to ₹1,500 on the Mar-Q result, maintaining Buy, while flagging a mixed quarter (revenue/EBITDA beat, PAT miss on higher depreciation, finance costs, and elevated minority interest attributed to a one-off). Management guided 23% organic growth and 100bps EBITDA margin expansion in FY27, with growth anchored in consolidating acquisitions and scaling medtech distribution. Monarch's Aug 2024 note (PT ₹1,500, Buy) predates the IPO seasoning period and is now ~22 months stale — its "distribution excellence" framing was directionally right but adds little current signal. The real debate is not bull vs. bear but whether the promised margin expansion is structural or aspirational in a business where gross margins are inherently thin.

My own read: Entero is an interesting consolidation play in Indian pharma distribution — a sector that is deeply fragmented and where scale genuinely creates cost advantages. The IPO (Feb 2024) was richly priced on the promise of being the aggregator, and the story has advanced: acquisitions are in the fold, medtech is a higher-margin vertical that could structurally lift the blended margin over time. That said, I'd be cautious about the PAT quality. "Elevated minority interest" in an acquisition-heavy rollup is rarely a clean one-off — it often reflects the structural reality of buying businesses without full control. Similarly, rising depreciation and finance costs are the inevitable hangover of the inorganic ramp, and the question is whether operating leverage from revenue scaling covers them fast enough. The 23% organic growth guidance is ambitious; I'd watch the quarterly organic vs. inorganic revenue split closely. Jefferies' revised EPS (FY27 cut, FY28 raised) is a reasonable base case but embeds a lot of execution faith. If medtech scaling hits friction or integration costs persist, the FY28 payoff slides further out.

Jeff|260526.change: PT raised ₹1,350→₹1,500; Buy maintained. FY27 EPS cut on higher tax rate and depreciation; FY28 EPS raised on improving margin trajectory.
Jeff|260526.view:
This is the only fresh, data-rich view in the library and it deserves weight. Jefferies' PT raise despite a PAT miss and FY27 EPS cut signals confidence in the medium-term trajectory over near-term noise — that's a defensible call if the margin expansion story holds.

However, I'd push back on the "one-off" characterisation of the minority interest drag. In rollup businesses, minority stakes are often structurally sticky until buy-out, and the cost of financing those buy-outs (via debt or dilution) is itself a risk to the FY28 EPS recovery. The 100bps margin expansion guidance is the key watch — at pharma distribution's thin absolute margins, any execution shortfall is disproportionately visible in PAT.

Monarch|240816.change: Dated Aug 2024; no matching pdfdata entry. Trendlyne shows Monarch had PT ₹1,515 in Jun 2024 and ₹1,500 in Aug 2024 — a marginal TP trim, Buy maintained.
Monarch|240816.view: This note is ~22 months old and essentially stale as a current input. The "distribution excellence" thesis was the IPO-era buy case and the landscape has moved on — acquisitions have closed, medtech has been added, and a full year of listed-company results has accumulated. Monarch's current view on post-acquisition integration and the PAT trajectory is unknown from this library. Treat it as directional background, not active signal.

Eureka Forbes.summary:
Four houses cover Eureka Forbes; two are fresh (Kotak and Nomura, both dated 260520, post-4QFY26 results) and two are stale (ICICI from Nov 2025, East India from Sep 2024). **Kotak** is the most constructive — Buy, PT ₹700 unchanged — absorbing 3–6% EPS cuts on RM inflation via a rolled-forward DCF and flagging management's confidence in WP acceleration. **Nomura** is also Buy but more candid about cost pressure, cutting PT ₹629→₹600 after RM/sales rose ~214 bps q-q in 4Q; it leans on new categories (air purifiers, water softeners) as the incremental growth lever. **ICICI** (Nov 2025, TP ₹685, Buy) lowered its target from ₹735, presumably reflecting moderation in near-term growth — this note predates 4QFY26 and is now ~7 months old. **East India** initiated at Hold in Sep 2024 with a ₹536 PT; at 20+ months old it is essentially irrelevant to current positioning. The real debate is whether RM cost pressure is transient and whether new categories can sustain revenue CAGR once the WP-penetration impulse moderates — Kotak says yes comfortably, Nomura is more watchful, ICICI has yet to update post-results.

My own read: Eureka Forbes owns a genuinely durable franchise — the installed AMC base is a recurring-revenue engine most consumer peers lack, and WP under-penetration in India (sub-20% urban, near-zero rural at meaningful price points) gives the category a long runway. The sell-side's ₹600–700 target band implies the market is pricing in ~12–15% volume CAGR plus steady margin expansion — both plausible but not guaranteed simultaneously. What the bulls are glossing over: RM inflation (steel, polymers) is structural enough to require pricing action, and Eureka's premium positioning limits how aggressively it can pass costs through in a competitive landscape that includes Kent, Havells, and AO Smith all investing in distribution. The new-categories thesis (air purifiers, softeners) is optionally exciting but remains sub-scale today. I'd sit close to Nomura's TP — cautiously constructive — and watch two things: (1) EBITDA margin trajectory over the next two quarters to confirm RM pressure is not worsening; (2) whether services revenue as a share of total crosses 35%+ (the threshold at which AMC recurring cash becomes a meaningful valuation re-rating driver).

Kotak|260520.change: PT unchanged ₹700; Buy maintained. FY2027/28E EPS cut 3–6% on RM inflation; DCF-based fair value rolled forward and held steady.
Kotak|260520.view:
Kotak's steady TP despite EPS cuts tells you the DCF model is absorbing near-term headwinds and discounting the WP penetration story at a long horizon — a defensible call, but it somewhat papers over the cost reality Nomura is more explicit about. The phrase 'management remains confident' recurs, which is a mild yellow flag; management guidance on WP acceleration has historically run ahead of actual delivery in softer macro quarters.

The 12%+ three-year WP volume CAGR is the key metric to anchor to. If that holds through FY27, Kotak's TP is reasonable; if it dips to mid-single digits (which RM-driven consumer fatigue could cause), the DCF quickly erodes. Worth monitoring quarterly rather than anchoring to the annual story.

Nomura|260520.change: PT cut ₹629→₹600; Buy maintained. RM/sales rose ~214 bps q-q to 41.3% in 4QFY26, only partially offset by lower other expenses.
Nomura|260520.view:
Nomura's TP cut is the more intellectually honest call in this earnings cycle — it names the specific RM headwind and adjusts rather than rolling a DCF. Buy at ₹600 is still a reasonable risk/reward if you believe the category remains structurally under-penetrated, but the new-categories lever (air purifiers, water softeners) that Nomura is using to justify 'growth momentum' is still unproven at scale.

The note is useful as a near-term sanity check: if RM/sales doesn't start to ease over the next 1–2 quarters, a further TP trim is plausible and Nomura will likely be the first to move. Watch the quarterly gross-margin line closely.

ICICI|251116.change: No pdfdata match for this note. Prior Trendlyne entry (Dec 2024): TP ₹735, Buy; current note (Nov 2025): TP ₹685, Buy — implies a TP cut of ₹735→₹685 between the two reports, Buy maintained throughout.
ICICI|251116.view: This note is now ~7 months old and pre-dates 4QFY26 results — the RM pressure and TP cuts from Kotak/Nomura have already moved the conversation forward. ICICI's 'under-penetration' thesis is the right structural frame and their gradual TP reduction (₹660 Oct 2024 → ₹735 Dec 2024 → ₹685 Nov 2025) shows they've been modestly recalibrating rather than blindly bullish. That said, the note is too stale to drive a current view. Treat as directionally consistent with the buy case but defer to the fresher Kotak/Nomura reads for near-term guidance.

East|240916.change: Initiation note dated Sep 2024 — no prior East India report in the library or Trendlyne to compare. No more recent note found from this house.
East|240916.view: At 20+ months old and with a ₹536 PT that sits well below the current ₹600–700 consensus cluster, this Hold initiation is effectively a historical artefact. East India's caution at initiation in Sep 2024 was understandable — new entrant to coverage, conservative valuation methodology — but the stock has re-rated materially since then. There is no current signal from this house; ignore for positioning purposes unless a fresh note emerges.

FSN E-commerce Ventures.summary:
Six houses cover Nykaa actively; the consensus leans bullish with one clear Neutral dissent. **Jefferies** (Buy/₹350) and **Nomura** (Buy/₹317) are the most constructive and both raised targets post-Q4FY26 results. **CLSA** (Outperform/₹338) and **Morgan Stanley** (OW, no TP in latest note) round out the bulls. **Kotak** (Add/₹300) is constructively cautious — sees quality but not deep mispricing. **JPMorgan** (Neutral/₹270) is the lone active hold, the lowest TP in the set, and the most explicit on valuation risk. **Geojit** (Accumulate/₹277, Dec 2025) is materially stale — predates the Q4FY26 results. Target spread among fresh notes: ₹270–₹350, with the bull cluster at ₹300–₹350. The real debate is not on operational trajectory — 28% revenue growth, 8.4% EBITDA margin (record), and Fashion EBITDA breakeven are broadly agreed milestones — but on how much of the improvement is already in the price.

My own read: Nykaa is a genuinely differentiated franchise in Indian beauty e-commerce — first-mover brand equity, a sticky own-brands engine (~54% YoY growth) that is both the margin lever and the competitive moat, and a customer repeat-purchase flywheel that is hard to replicate. The Q4FY26 print was legitimately impressive. That said, the sell-side is too uniformly cheerful about Fashion. Fashion EBITDA breakeven in one quarter — achieved partly through marketing efficiency — is not the same as a durable structural turn. Fashion competes directly against Myntra (Flipkart-backed) and Ajio (Reliance-backed), both better-resourced and willing to subsidise growth; one quarter of marketing restraint can flip back negative. The more important watch is **own-brand penetration in Beauty** (the real moat and re-rating driver) and **competitive pressure from Tira** (Reliance's beauty vertical, still early but backed by deep pockets). JPMorgan's Neutral at ₹270 is the most intellectually honest call in the set — it acknowledges the operational improvement while noting current multiples leave limited margin of safety. I'd land closer to Kotak's Add than to Jefferies' aggressive Buy at stiff valuations.

MorganStan|260602.change: PT not disclosed in this note; OW maintained. This is a conference feedback note (India Investment Forum 2026), not a full valuation report — no TP appears in the PDF data.
MorganStan|260602.view: Morgan Stanley's OW is conviction-based but this note adds little new valuation work — it is a management channel check from the firm's own investor forum. The key themes they surfaced: Beauty focused on customer acquisition and purchase frequency; Fashion on curating the right brands and customers. The 'right kind of customers' framing for Fashion is worth noting — it signals management is being selective on Fashion cohorts, the correct strategic call, but one that implicitly limits Fashion's total addressable scale. Weight this note primarily as a sentiment confirmation of MS's existing OW stance rather than a fresh thesis.

CLSA|260522.change: First captured CLSA report in the library — no prior to compare. TP ₹338, Outperform.
CLSA|260522.view: CLSA's Outperform is substantively argued: 28% revenue growth, highest-ever 8.4% EBITDA margin (+195bps YoY), EBITDA 8% above consensus, and own brands up 54% YoY driving margin accretion. The Fashion EBITDA breakeven is correctly flagged as a milestone. One caveat they noted: EBIT missed their estimate due to higher-than-expected depreciation — a structural item to track as Nykaa scales capex in warehousing and tech infrastructure. CLSA's ₹338 TP sits mid-range of the bullish cluster, suggesting they see a clear re-rating path but are not the most aggressive buyer in the group.

JP|260522.change: PT held at ₹270; Neutral maintained — no change vs prior.
JP|260522.view:
JPMorgan is the lone active Neutral in this coverage universe, with a ₹270 target well below the ₹300–₹350 range of the bulls. They acknowledge Q4 EBITDA beat and Fashion's first EBITDA-positive quarter but their Neutral signals the good news is priced in at current levels.

This is arguably the most disciplined call in the set. Nykaa trades at a significant premium to growth peers and JPMorgan's pushback on valuation deserves respect even as the operational trajectory is positive. If the stock re-rated sharply post-Q4 results, JP's ₹270 target implies meaningful downside risk on any execution miss. The key question to watch: at what forward EBITDA multiple does the stock screen, and is the margin expansion trajectory fast enough to justify it? JPMorgan's implicit answer is no, for now.

Kotak|260522.change: First captured Kotak report in the library — no prior to compare. TP ₹300, Add.
Kotak|260522.view:
Kotak's Add is measured optimism. They correctly highlighted BPC contribution margin and EBITDA margin expansion 'despite aggressive investment in customer acquisition' — an important qualifier showing quality of the margin beat — and Fashion EBITDA turning positive. The Add (rather than Buy) rating and ₹300 TP signals they see quality but not sufficient mispricing to go outright bullish.

Kotak is well-regarded for Indian consumer/internet research and their restraint relative to Jefferies is informative. The ₹300 target implies a reasonable medium-term path but not a deeply undervalued situation. This is probably the most balanced house view in the set for someone sizing a position — acknowledges the positives without ignoring valuation.

Jeff|260521.view:
Jefferies is the most bullish voice and the most openly valuation-agnostic — they acknowledge 'stiff valuations' explicitly but argue strong growth supports them. Their insight that Fashion breaking EBITDA even signals management 'cracked the code' is the most structurally important call: if Fashion sustains EBITDA positivity, it removes a drag that has weighed on the investment case for years and significantly changes the group P&L narrative.

I'd stress-test the durability of Fashion breakeven: it was achieved partly through marketing cost discipline (14.3% of sales vs estimates ~15%), which can reverse quickly in a competitive quarter. Jefferies' ₹350 is the most aspirational target in the set — it assumes the margin expansion trajectory continues and the market keeps paying a premium multiple. Worth holding if you believe in the own-brand moat, but the upside-to-downside at ₹350 is narrower than Jefferies implies.

Nomura|260521.view:
Nomura's Buy is grounded in the Q4 margin beat — EBITDA of 8.4% vs their 7.6% estimate, and lower-than-expected marketing costs (14.3% actual vs 15.2% estimate). They are focused on the margin lever story, the right analytical framing: Nykaa's re-rating ultimately depends on sustainable margin expansion, not just GMV momentum.

Nomura's detailed margin disaggregation (RM/sales, marketing costs, EBIT margin line by line) makes this the most technically rigorous note in the set. Their ₹317 TP is more conservative than Jefferies but still above JPMorgan's ₹270. The risk to their Buy: if marketing costs mean-revert higher (they are currently running below historical averages), EBITDA margin could undershoot next quarter and trigger a re-rating in reverse.

Geojit|251211.change: Downgraded Buy→Accumulate; TP ₹277 (Dec 2025). Prior Trendlyne entry (May 2024): Buy at ₹186. No more recent Geojit report in the library — this note is ~6 months old as of Jun 2026.
Geojit|251211.view: Geojit's Dec 2025 Accumulate is materially stale — it predates the Q4FY26 results that drove the bullish re-rating from peers, and it predates Fashion's first EBITDA-positive print. Their ₹277 TP now sits below even JPMorgan's Neutral ₹270 target and well below the ₹300–₹350 range of updated notes. The downgrade from Buy in May 2024 (at ₹186) to Accumulate in Dec 2025 (at ₹277) likely reflected valuation stretch at that point in time. Discount this view heavily; it is not representative of the post-Q4FY26 picture.

Finolex Cables.summary:
Jefferies (Jun 2026, Buy ₹1,200) is the sole fresh and outright bull in the coverage — raising its PT from ₹1,000 to ₹1,200 after a strong Mar-Q beat and citing the stock still trading at ~19x FY27 PE, in-line with its 10-year historical average despite a +30% YTD run. The remaining three houses are materially staler: Geojit downgraded to Accumulate (Mar 2026, PT ₹1,008), Anand Rathi maintained Buy but cut PT to ₹975 (Nov 2025), and Sharekhan's Buy at ₹1,650 (Aug 2024) is nearly two years old and effectively vestigial. The real tension is between Jefferies' valuation-anchored bull case and the Geojit/AR cluster whose targets sit at or below current market price — making them inadvertent Sell signals rather than constructive views. No broker carries a formal Sell; the bear case is expressed purely through stale or below-CMP price targets.

My own read: Finolex is a credible franchise — among the stronger brands in Indian wires and cables, benefiting from housing/infra tailwinds and disciplined price-hike pass-through (~20% in FY26 to offset copper). The +30% YTD rally looks earnings-driven rather than re-rating-driven if Jefferies' 21x FY27 PE is accurate, and that multiple being in-line with the historical mean is a fair base case. That said, the concentration risk is real: ~85% of revenue is in electrical cables, making the stock highly sensitive to copper price trajectory and housing-cycle duration. The persistent FMEG drag (fans, switches) has been improving toward positive EBIT but remains a value detractor until it scales. I'd monitor the OFC opportunity closely — optical fibre cable is a genuine growth vector if government broadband rollout accelerates, but it's early. On balance, Jefferies is the only view worth running with today; the rest of the coverage needs refreshing before drawing conclusions.

Jeff|260601.view:
The freshest and most substantive note in the coverage. The valuation argument holds up — 21x/18x FY27/28e PE at or below the 10-year average, while the operational picture is improving (cable volumes healthy across Auto, Flexible, Power; ~20% cumulative price hikes in FY26 passing copper costs through; FMEG turning positive EBIT). The ₹1,200 PT implies a meaningful premium to the Geojit/AR cluster and is the only call that currently offers real upside if correct.

The risks Jefferies underplays: copper is the central variable — Finolex is a price-taker on input costs, and any reversal of the pass-through ability (competitive pressure from newer entrants like Polycab, KEI) would quickly compress margins. The OFC bet is worth watching but modest in the near term. I'd track the Q1 FY27 volume numbers and whether FY27 EPS delivery stays on track; if so, the ₹1,200 target is reasonable.

Geojit|260318.change: Downgraded Buy→Accumulate; PT nudged ₹988 (Oct 2025)→₹1,008 (Mar 2026). No pdfdata entry; derived from trendlyne.
Geojit|260318.view:
A downgrade paired with a token PT raise is a textbook conviction-trimming move — Geojit is essentially saying the easy money has been made. With a PT of ₹1,008 in March 2026 and the stock subsequently running +30% YTD (per Jefferies' June note), this Accumulate has almost certainly become a de-facto Sell relative to CMP. The note is now three months old and likely below the current price.

Geojit's PT history tells a story of persistent conservatism: ₹1,019 (Mar 2024) → ₹1,354 (Dec 2024, Accumulate) → ₹988 (Oct 2025, Buy on the dip) → ₹1,008 (Mar 2026, back to Accumulate as it rallied). They've oscillated between Buy and Accumulate across the cycle without conviction. I'd treat the Geojit view as a cautious valuation cap rather than a directional call, and note it needs updating before any weight can be placed on it.

AR|251124.change: PT cut ₹1,031→₹975; Buy maintained. Note dated Nov 2025 — over 6 months old.
AR|251124.view:
Anand Rathi has been persistently bullish through a steep PT compression cycle: from ₹1,577 (Nov 2024) to ₹1,031 (Aug 2025) to ₹975 (Nov 2025). The 'mixed performance, steady H2 recovery' thesis from November appears to have partially played out — Jefferies' Mar-Q note flags a strong quarter. But at ₹975, AR's PT is well below Jefferies' ₹1,200, and almost certainly below CMP given the +30% YTD move.

This note is effectively stale and its PT inadvertently signals downside. The persistent Buy rating despite cut-upon-cut-upon-cut PTs suggests AR may be anchoring to an outdated earnings model. I'd assign low weight until AR refreshes with post-Mar-Q numbers.

Sharekhan|240819.change: PT cut ₹1,800→₹1,650; Buy maintained. Note dated Aug 2024 — nearly 2 years old.
Sharekhan|240819.view: Entirely stale — this predates the full copper-volatility-driven margin compression, the FY25 earnings cuts, and the subsequent recovery. Sharekhan has not published a follow-up visible in the data. The ₹1,650 PT is above even Jefferies' current bull case of ₹1,200, reflecting market conditions from a different phase of the cycle entirely. Ignore for current thesis purposes; check whether Sharekhan still actively covers the stock.

Finolex Industries.summary:
The four houses covering Finolex Industries post-Q4FY26 split into two clear camps. **Jefferies** (Buy, PT ₹220, raised from ₹195) and **Anand Rathi** (Buy, PT ₹240) are constructive — both see favourable risk/reward after a margin beat in Q4 (OPM ~25% vs ~14.6% the prior year), with Jefferies framing it as an Agri/rural and plumbing-mix-upgrade play at a ~19x FY27E multiple in line with the 10-year historical average. **Prabhudas Lilladhar** downgraded to Accumulate (PT ₹207, cut from ₹228), judging the margin beat as partly inventory-driven and volumes too subdued to warrant a Buy. **BOB Capital** holds its Hold/₹190 from February — effectively the bear anchor after cutting from Buy in late 2025 — and has not moved despite the Q4 beat. **IDBI Capital**'s Hold predates the Q4 results by nearly 10 months and is stale. The real debate is whether the ~25% Q4 OPM reflects a durable cost reset or a one-quarter inventory/spread gain, and whether FY27 volumes recover after FY26's 4% decline.

My own read: Finolex is fundamentally a commodity processor — it buys PVC resin (imported, USD-priced) and converts it to pipes. When resin prices ease or inventory spreads are favourable, OPM spikes; when they normalise, OPM collapses. The Q4 beat looks at least partly mechanical in that context, which is what PL and BOB are pricing in. The agri pipe skew (~65% of volume mix) makes the business weather-dependent and cyclical around rural spend; the pivot toward plumbing/fittings (~37% now, targeting ~50% over five years) is the right strategy but is a multi-year execution story facing better-capitalised incumbents — Astral Poly, Supreme Industries, Prince Pipes. At ~19x FY27E the stock is at its long-run mean: fair, but not cheap enough to provide a buffer if volumes disappoint again. I would want to see sustained FY27 volume growth — not just another margin print — and preferably two consecutive strong plumbing-segment quarters before adding conviction. For now I would sit roughly in line with PL's Accumulate stance: fine to hold, but the asymmetry for a fresh Buy is not yet compelling.

BOB|260529.change: Hold maintained at ₹190; unchanged vs the Feb 2026 prior note (also Hold/₹190). BOB cut from Buy (PT ₹240) to Hold (PT ₹190) in its February 2026 note — the current update makes no adjustment despite the Q4 margin beat.
BOB|260529.view:
BOB Capital has traced a full disappointment arc on this stock: Buy at ₹265 (May 2025) → Buy at ₹240 (Nov 2025) → Hold at ₹190 (Feb 2026) → Hold at ₹190 today. The flat update after a strong Q4 print speaks volumes; they are not persuaded the beat changes the volume trajectory.
