PL|260527.change: Downgraded from Hold to Reduce; PT raised ₹26,108→₹30,768 (trendlyne; prior note was initiation of coverage dated Mar 2026, Hold).
PL|260527.view:
Prabhudas Lilladhar's Reduce with a simultaneously raised PT is the most intellectually honest call in this cohort: they acknowledge the structural growth story is intact and numbers are going up, but argue the stock has re-rated so aggressively that the risk/reward has flipped negative. This is a valuation call, not a thesis reversal — and those are often the most durable.

The Reduce at ₹30,768 effectively says 'good business, wrong price right now.' If the CMP is materially above that level, PL's call is the most actionable downside flag here. I'd take it seriously as a counter-weight to Jefferies' optimism. Watch for whether PL raises the target further in coming quarters with the rating maintained — a series of upward PT revisions while staying Reduce would confirm the structural bull is running ahead of fundamentals.

Geojit|250812.change: Upgraded from Sell to Hold; PT raised ₹16,853→₹22,859 (trendlyne; prior note dated May 2025). This note is approximately 10 months old — treat as stale.
Geojit|250812.view:
The Geojit note from August 2025 is the oldest in this set by a wide margin and offers no current guidance. At ₹22,859, the PT is the lowest of all six houses and is almost certainly far below the current market price given the stock's trajectory since mid-2025. The upgrade from Sell to Hold was probably correct at the time.

Disregard for any current positioning decision. It remains only as a data point showing how dramatically the stock has re-rated since August 2025 — the distance between Geojit's stale ₹22,859 and Jefferies' current ₹43,145 captures the extent of that re-rating.

Honasa Consumer.summary:
Three active post-Q4FY26 houses are all bullish: **Jefferies** (Buy, ₹565), **Kotak** (Add, ₹455), and **CLSA** (Outperform, ₹434). A fourth, **ICICI Securities** (Buy, ₹400), is directionally aligned but stale from Aug 2025. The salient move since Q4 reporting is Kotak's Jun 2026 Investor Day update, which lifted its TP further from ₹405 to ₹455 after management laid out an FY31 vision targeting high-teens revenue CAGR and 100bps annual EBITDA margin expansion. Targets cluster at ₹434–455 for CLSA/Kotak, with Jefferies as the clear outlier at ₹565. There is no active bear in the covered houseViews set — though JPMorgan (not represented here) remains Underweight at ₹365, just above the current stock price, the one voice keeping the bull consensus honest. The real debate is not whether the FY26 operational recovery is genuine (broadly accepted) but whether the multi-year compounding story justifies the current multiple.

My own read: Honasa's pivot — A&P concentration on focus categories, distribution architecture overhaul, brand rationalisation — has delivered tangible results: Q4 LFL organic growth of 21%, 650bps YoY EBITDA margin expansion, and younger brands growing at 28% YoY. The Investor Day FY31 roadmap signals management confidence, but it also sets a demanding bar. Jefferies' ₹565 target embeds a near-fully-delivered compounding story and feels stretched until at least two more consistent FY27 quarters confirm the trajectory; Kotak at ₹455 is the more honest calibration. The two things I'd watch most: (1) whether the 100bps/year EBITDA margin delivery sustains as scale grows and competitive intensity from Minimalist and Pilgrim picks up; and (2) whether JPMorgan's UW thesis — the only major persistent bear — starts to narrow, which would be the clearest signal the consensus rerating is earned.

Kotak|260611.change: PT raised ₹405→₹455; Add maintained (Jun 2026, post-Investor Day note).
Kotak|260611.view:
The Investor Day note is a strategic update rather than a quarterly beat call — Kotak is signalling increasing conviction in the FY31 roadmap (high-teens revenue CAGR, distribution deepening, younger brands as a second engine). The ₹50 TP lift (~12%) is incremental, not a multiple-expansion call, which is the right register for a company still mid-execution.

Kotak at ₹455 sits between CLSA (₹434) and Jefferies (₹565), representing the most calibrated bull position in the set. They were constructive post-Q4 and became more so after the Investor Day — a coherent progression. The key test is whether management's FY31 targets survive the first signs of FY27 delivery; any shortfall in H1FY27 EBITDA margins would put this TP under pressure before the year is out.

CLSA|260522.view: CLSA is constructively bullish post Q4, anchoring the call on the 650bps YoY EBITDA margin expansion and Mamaearth's teens-growth trajectory. Their ₹434 PT is conservative relative to Jefferies, suggesting CLSA is valuing closer to near-term earnings rather than pricing in full compounding optionality. The "strong beat across the board" framing is fair — both revenue and margin came in ahead of estimates — but CLSA is not extrapolating the beat into a structural rerating story. I would view their Outperform as the most measured bull position among the post-Q4 set: positive on execution, cautious on multiple expansion.

Jeff|260521.view:
Jefferies is the most bullish house by a wide margin at ₹565, and their framing — "where there's a will, there's a way" — reflects high conviction in management execution. The compounding story they outline (high-teens revenue CAGR + 100bps annual EBITDA margin expansion over five years) is the most useful analytical framework: if delivered, it implies EBITDA margins moving from ~11% today toward 15–16%, which would justify a meaningful rerating.

Whether Jefferies is too optimistic depends entirely on whether that 100bps/year is credible at scale. The Q4 beat was real, but a single quarter's margin outperformance is not the same as a structural cost curve shift. I would give Jefferies credit for being the first to frame this as a compounding story and for raising PT from ₹500 to ₹565 before consensus caught up — but I would watch the first two quarters of FY27 closely before adopting the full ₹565 view.

ICICI|250813.change: No pdfdata match. Trendlyne shows TP ₹400, Buy (Aug 2025); prior trendlyne entry (Jun 2025) also shows TP ₹400, Buy — no change between the two. Note is approximately 10 months old as of Jun 2026.
ICICI|250813.view: The ICICI note predates the strong Q4FY26 results and the subsequent PT raises by the other houses. At Buy, ₹400 it is directionally correct but stale — written when the recovery thesis was less proven. The headline from Aug 2025 is now vindicated by what actually played out in FY26, but the specific TP and analysis are outdated. Discount the ₹400 figure; this note adds limited information relative to the three active post-Q4 reports.

Hyundai Motor India.summary:
Three of four houses are constructive on Hyundai Motor India: **JPMorgan** (OW, PT ₹2,135, May-2026), **BOB Capital** (Buy, PT ₹2,261, May-2026), and **ICICI** (Buy, PT ₹2,150, Mar-2026), with targets clustered in a narrow ₹2,135–2,261 band. **Emkay** is the sole dissenter — a Reduce at ₹1,750 from its Oct-2024 IPO-era initiation, now over 18 months stale. The bulls share a common theme: management is constructive on near-term PV demand (GST-cut tailwind), commodity inflation is manageable via multiple levers, and new model launches beyond the Creta/Venue core can regain market share. The real debate is between this product-pipeline optimism and Emkay's original concern that valuation already priced in a recovery that hadn't materialised — HMIL has ceded ground to Tata and Mahindra in the mid-SUV segment it pioneered. BOB's recent modest TP trim (₹2,287→₹2,261) and the qualitative CXO-series tone from JPMorgan hint that even the bulls are tempering near-term expectations.

My own read: HMIL is a high-quality franchise — India's second-largest PV network, a strong brand in the ₹10–25L SUV band, and a parent that can localise profitably. But the market-share erosion story is genuinely concerning: Mahindra's sustained SUV wave and Tata's domestically-developed EV and SUV pipeline are compressing exactly the space HMIL used to own by default. The GST-cut tailwind is real but temporary; what matters is whether 'filling whitespaces' (ICICI's thesis) actually lands — whether HMIL can launch competitive models at pace rather than harvesting the Creta halo. I'd want to see two or three successful new-model launches before fully buying the re-acceleration story. At current bull-target levels the market is already pricing in recovery, so downside on a miss is asymmetric — Emkay's valuation concern, however stale the note, names the right risk. The two things I'd watch most: Q1–Q2 FY27 volume market share (does the GST cut lift all boats, or disproportionately help HMIL?), and the reception of any new SUV entries in the ₹12–18L segment.

JP|260526.change: PT ₹2,135; OW. First JPMorgan report captured in the library (prevCall null) — a post-CXO fireside-chat note, not a formal model update, so there is no prior TP or rating delta to report.
JP|260526.view:
The fireside chat with HMIL's MD & CEO confirms management is leaning into the GST-cut tailwind and flagging commodity inflation as manageable — a credible, near-term constructive read straight from the top. JPMorgan's OW at ₹2,135 is the freshest coverage in the library and carries weight as a top-tier global house with deep auto-sector resources.

The note is qualitative rather than a full model update, so the TP hasn't moved and earnings revisions (if any) aren't visible here. Treat this as a useful sentiment data point from management — confirmatory of the bull thesis, but softer evidence than a model-driven call. Watch whether JPMorgan follows with a formal update after Q1 FY27 results.

BOB|260509.change: PT trimmed ₹2,287→₹2,261; Buy maintained (vs. BOB's initiation on 24-Mar-2026).
BOB|260509.view:
BOB initiated in March 2026 on a capacity-ramp thesis and has now nudged the PT down 1% — a marginal trim, not a conviction shift. The 'snag in the short term' language acknowledges near-term execution risk (capacity ramp, possible demand lumpiness post-GST cut) without abandoning the structural bull case.

BOB is a smaller domestic house; its coverage adds breadth to the house-view picture rather than differentiated modelling edge. The TP trim is the most recent directional signal from any house in the library and is worth logging, but I'd weight the JPMorgan and ICICI views more heavily on substance.

ICICI|260331.change: PT ₹2,150; Buy. No earlier ICICI report in the library to compare — dated Mar-2026.
ICICI|260331.view:
ICICI's 'Beyond Creta-Venue' report is the most substantive medium-term bull thesis in the library: the argument that HMIL can use whitespace model launches (segments it doesn't currently contest) to arrest market share erosion. This is the pivotal debate — HMIL's domestic product cadence has been slower than Tata's or Mahindra's organically developed SUVs.

The Buy at ₹2,150 is credible but now nearly three months old, and the execution of new launches (timing, pricing, consumer reception) is the key variable. The thesis weakens materially if new models disappoint or if Mahindra/Tata continue expanding aggressively in the ₹10–20L SUV band. Track new-model announcements and early booking data as the acid test of ICICI's core argument.

Emkay|241022.change: Initiation in Oct-2024; Reduce, PT ₹1,750. Over 18 months old — no subsequent Emkay update in the library.
Emkay|241022.view:
Emkay was the lone bear at IPO, flagging that HMIL's franchise quality doesn't justify the valuation premium versus PV peers at listing prices. The core concern — strong brand, but muted volume growth and a rich multiple — remains structurally relevant: HMIL has been losing market share since listing. At ₹1,750 the Reduce call sat ~25–30% below where the current bull targets cluster, implying Emkay anticipated either a de-rating or a growth miss that hasn't fully played out yet.

This note is too stale to act on directly, but the valuation-vs-growth tension it identifies is still the right analytical framework. Until Emkay publishes an update — whether to close the call or double down — treat this as a live reminder of the bear case rather than a live rating. If HMIL's new launches disappoint, this thesis has the most to say.

Delhivery.summary:
Eight houses are on record — seven with explicit Buy/OW ratings and one (Jefferies) with a sector-level logistics preview note that carries no company rating. Active targets cluster at ₹534–₹610; the Geojit (Dec-2025, ₹469) and ICICI (Nov-2025, ₹600) prints are best treated as stale baselines. JPMorgan raised PT ₹600→₹610 and held OW after Q4FY26 results; Motilal Oswal raised ₹570→₹580; **Prabhudas Lilladhar upgraded outright from Accumulate to Buy**, moving PT ₹466→₹534 — FCF-positivity was their explicit gating condition. **Kotak alone trimmed PT** (₹590→₹580), reflecting valuation discipline rather than thesis deterioration. The real debate is not direction — all are broadly constructive — but pace: how fast does FCF compound from the FY26 inflection, and can Express Parcel EBITDA margins hold above 18% at scale?

My own read: the FCF inflection is genuine — ₹890mn in FY26 versus –₹2,520mn in FY25 is a real regime shift for a business that burned cash for four years post-IPO. The 16% ROIC in Express + PTL (pre-tax, pre-CWIP) at Q4FY26 run-rate signals the network has crossed the density threshold where returns start compounding. What the sell-side underweights: the 73% Q4 volume growth partly reflects a one-time consolidation windfall as smaller players ceded share — sustaining that trajectory requires winning fresh outsourcing mandates, which gets harder. Yield-per-shipment in Q1FY27 is the clearest canary; a tariff war with captive arms compresses margins faster than volume. Kotak's inflation/GST compliance structural-edge argument is under-appreciated: regulatory burden on unorganised captive logistics is rising, and Delhivery's formalised scale benefits disproportionately. I'd be constructive but value-conscious above ₹580 — the upside from here requires the FY28 FCF scale-up to arrive on schedule.

Jeff|260520.change: Sector logistics preview note (May-2026); no company-specific TP or rating for Delhivery in this report.
Jeff|260520.view: This is a ports-and-logistics sector data note, not a Delhivery company call. Jefferies is tracking macro indicators — port container volumes up 7% YoY, railway freight down 7% YoY, truck freight rates soft — and Delhivery appears in the coverage universe by sector association, not by rating action. The soft truck freight rates are a mild competitive positive for Delhivery's road-express pricing, but Jefferies does not connect the dots explicitly. Do not read this as a directional stance on the stock.

JP|260518.view:
JP's Q4FY26 note is the most substantive write-up in the library. The FCF-positive headline ('Here comes the FCF') is well-chosen — this was the milestone sceptics had waited for. The 18.8% Express service EBITDA margin (vs. 15.9% a year ago) is the most important single data point: it suggests margin expansion has structural legs beyond near-term volume leverage.

The marginal PT raise (₹600→₹610) is conservative relative to JP's bullish tone, likely reflecting an open terminal-value question — what multiple does a FCF-compounding Indian logistics platform deserve? I find the FCF thesis credible, but JP does not stress-test yield assumptions against a scenario where Amazon or Meesho materially expand captive last-mile. That gap is the main thing I'd push on.

Kotak|260518.view:
Kotak's PT trim in the face of strong results is the most interesting signal in this Q4FY26 batch. It is not a thesis capitulation — Buy is maintained — but it reflects disciplined DCF anchoring: the 16% ROIC (pre-tax, pre-CWIP) is approaching but not yet firmly above a typical WACC, which caps how aggressively you can raise the target.

Kotak's most valuable contribution is the inflation/statutory cost-edge argument: rising minimum wages and GST compliance costs hurt unorganised captive logistics harder than Delhivery's formalised, scale-efficient network. This structural advantage compounds quietly and the market is not pricing it explicitly. I would weight this angle highly in any bear-case stress test — it makes the moat more durable than volume-share charts alone suggest.

PL|260518.change: Rating upgraded from Accumulate to Buy; PT raised ₹466→₹534.
PL|260518.view:
PL's upgrade is the most significant rating event in this result round. Their prior Accumulate at ₹466 (Aug-2025) flagged B2C volume uncertainty; the FCF-positive print clearly crossed their threshold, and the title 'Turns FCFF positive' says exactly what moved them.

The ₹534 PT still lags JP/MO/ICICI, suggesting PL is running a more conservative FCF model or a lower exit multiple. I'd treat the upgrade as a positive sentiment signal — a previously cautious house now onboard — but not as a PT anchor. PL's ₹534 is already being left behind by peers and would likely be revised upward in a follow-up note.

MO|260517.view:
Motilal has been consistently bullish since at least Jan-2026 — Buy through the Q2FY26 margin miss and the broader logistics de-rating. The marginal PT raise post-Q4 (₹570→₹580) is incremental; MO's core thesis ('structurally best placed in e-commerce logistics consolidation') is unchanged.

The risk is consistency-as-conviction conflation: MO has been Buy for 6+ months without a step-change PT revision, which makes it hard to tell whether Q4FY26 results substantively updated their model or whether they are anchored. The outsourcing-to-3PL theme is directionally correct, but the pace and scale of mandates from large e-commerce players is the variable to watch — and MO is not granular on this.

Emkay|260307.view:
Emkay's March note predates Q4FY26 results by two months and is now stale. Their consolidation thesis — industry rationalisation supporting B2C volume recovery — has since played out strongly (73% Q4 volume growth). The slight PT trim to ₹500 at the time likely reflected near-term uncertainty around consolidation timing rather than a structural concern.

Given Q4's beat, Emkay's ₹500 PT would almost certainly be revised upward in a post-results update. Do not weight the absolute TP; the consolidation thesis they identified was correct and early.

Geojit|251226.change: Upgraded to Buy with PT ₹469 on Dec-2025. No prior Geojit call in the library to compare.
Geojit|251226.view: Stale (Dec-2025) and well below the current consensus PT range. Geojit's upgrade was a catch-up move — they were behind peers who had been at Buy for much longer. The ₹469 TP is materially outdated given Q4FY26's strong results and the subsequent PT revisions. This note is of historical interest (documenting a laggard house finally upgrading) but should not be used as a current price anchor.

ICICI|251106.change: PT ₹600; Buy maintained. TP unchanged vs Aug-2025 prior.
ICICI|251106.view:
ICICI's Nov-2025 note is 7 months old and predates Q4FY26 results. Their 'structural tailwinds + strong execution = rerating' framing was prescient — the story has broadly played out. The ₹600 PT was set before FCF turned positive, meaning ICICI was pre-pricing the FCF inflection; in that sense their thesis has been validated.

Without a post-Q4FY26 update it is unclear whether ICICI still sees upside to ₹600 at current levels or would raise it given the FCF beat. Stale for trading purposes, but watch for a refresh after Q1FY27 results — if they reiterate Buy at ₹600+ post-results, that would be a stronger conviction signal.

IPCA Laboratories.summary:
All five covering houses are bullish — no bear or neutral in the set. The fresher pair, **PL** (Jun-2026, ₹1,800) and **Nomura** (May-2026, ₹1,725), bracket a tight cluster around ₹1,750–1,800. **ICICI Direct** upgraded to Buy at ₹1,660 in Nov-2025 — directionally aligned but its target has since been passed. **Motilal Oswal** (₹1,980, Dec-2024) and **Sharekhan** (₹1,765, Nov-2024) are 18-month-old notes; their targets were set before the FY26 margin recovery played out and carry limited current signal. The real debate has essentially collapsed: the Q4FY26 print — EBITDA +20% y-y, gross margin +257bp, India +12%, export formulations +16% — validated the turnaround thesis most houses had been building toward. PL's explicit "strong FY27 guidance" flag is the forward pivot point; the question is no longer whether the recovery happened but whether guidance converts.

My own read: IPCA is a solid mid-cap pharma franchise that spent FY24–25 digesting the Unichem merger and delivering disappointingly flat margins — the upgrade cycle (PL moved from Accumulate ₹1,525 in mid-2025 to Buy ₹1,800 by Mar-2026) tracks the operational recovery closely and feels earned, not premature. The chronic-therapy domestic position is sticky and the formulations-mix shift (76% of export sales now, up from 73% a year ago) is the right structural direction for margins. What the sell-side is glossing over: US generic revenues remain lumpy and molecule-concentrated — Nomura flags the beat there but IPCA's US history is one of niche wins followed by pricing attrition; any ANDA setback or US customer concentration risk would unwind the export-led thesis quickly. The Unichem working capital burden also lingers. I'd be broadly aligned with the bulls — the margin trajectory is real — but I'd want to see two quarters of H1FY27 delivery on management's guidance before attaching much weight to PL's ₹1,800 or MO's now-vintage ₹1,980. The two things I'd watch: (1) quarterly US revenue trend and gross margin direction; (2) H1FY27 earnings vs the "strong FY27 guidance" bar PL cited.

PL|260602.change: PT ₹1,800 maintained; Buy maintained (unchanged vs Mar-2026 note at ₹1,800/Buy; PL had previously upgraded from Accumulate ₹1,525 in mid-2025 to Buy ₹1,710 in Feb-2026 and further to ₹1,800 in Mar-2026).
PL|260602.view:
PL has been the most consistently tracked house across the FY26 cycle and its upgrade trajectory — Accumulate at ₹1,525 (mid-2025), Buy ₹1,710 (Feb-2026 Q3 beat), Buy ₹1,800 (Mar-2026 management meet), Buy ₹1,800 (Jun-2026 Q4 results) — reads as disciplined, step-by-step re-rating rather than a one-shot call. The Q4 note flagging "strong FY27 guidance" is the key line; PL is not just endorsing the Q4 beat but committing to the forward trajectory.

The risk is that ₹1,800 is a 0% move from the Mar-2026 target — PL chose not to raise even after a strong Q4 print, which could mean the target is being held pending H1FY27 confirmation, or that the stock has caught up with fair value. I'd treat this note as confirmation that the recovery is on track but watch for whether PL moves the target materially after Q1FY27 results.

Nomura|260531.change: PT ₹1,725 maintained; Buy maintained (pdfdata confirms prevTP ₹1,725 = currTP ₹1,725 and prevCall Buy = currCall Buy — no change vs prior Nomura note).
Nomura|260531.view:
Nomura's Q4FY26 note is the most data-rich in the set and worth reading carefully. The specific callouts — India +12% y-y ahead by 1%, export formulations +16% y-y driving mix to 76% (from 73%), gross margin 71% (+257bp y-y), EBITDA margin +229bp y-y, EBITDA +20% y-y — are genuinely strong numbers that are verifiable and precise.

Nomura's ₹1,725 target is ₹75 below PL's ₹1,800, implying it's more conservative on the FY27 ramp. The unchanged target after a beat suggests Nomura thinks the strong Q4 was already priced in. The formulations-mix focus is the right analytical lens: every percentage-point shift from API to branded formulations is structurally margin-accretive. I'd weight this note highly for quality; it's fresh, specific, and grounded in the actual result.

ICICI|251117.change: Upgraded to Buy with PT ₹1,660 on 17-Nov-2025; no earlier ICICI entry in the library to compare prior call or target.
ICICI|251117.view:
The ICICI upgrade at ₹1,660 is now about 7 months old and its target has been surpassed by both PL (₹1,800) and Nomura (₹1,725). The upgrade was likely triggered by Q2FY26 results and was probably a catch-up call after IPCA had already demonstrated early margin recovery signs. The ₹1,660 entry thesis — that IPCA was cheap vs pharma peers at that level — has played out.

This note is a directional signal, not a live price target. Without a fresh ICICI note post-Q4FY26, it offers limited current guidance. Treat as stale.

MO|241227.change: PT raised ₹1,950→₹1,980; Buy maintained (vs Oct-2024 note at ₹1,950/Buy per trendlyne).
MO|241227.view:
Motilal Oswal's Dec-2024 note carrying the highest target in the set (₹1,980) is now 18 months old — written before the FY26 margin recovery and well before the Q4FY26 data. The thesis pillars MO cited — US scaling and IPM (Indian Pharma Market) outperformance — are directionally validated by subsequent results, which is a mark in its favour, but the ₹1,980 target was set in a different earnings and valuation context.

The minimal PT move (₹1,950→₹1,980, a token raise) in Dec-2024 suggests MO was already near its then-fair-value estimate after the Oct upgrade. Without a post-FY26-results refresh, this note is primarily useful as historical context. MO clearly believed in the US ramp early; whether its model now looks more or less bullish than the ₹1,980 print implied depends on actual US revenue delivery, which later notes haven't quantified explicitly.

Sharekhan|241114.change: PT ₹1,765; Buy — no earlier Sharekhan entry in the library to compare prior call or target.
Sharekhan|241114.view:
The Sharekhan note from Nov-2024 predates the FY26 recovery and is 18+ months stale. The two thesis pillars it cited — US recovery and Unichem integration benefits — have since validated, and ₹1,765 was a reasonable target at the time. However, there has been no Sharekhan refresh in the library since; treat this as an early-cycle conviction call that has largely run its course.

Sharekhan's target is now sandwiched between ICICI (₹1,660) and Nomura (₹1,725) at stale context — the thesis is outdated enough that it adds little marginal information about the current risk/reward.

IRB Infrastructure.summary:
Two houses cover IRB Infrastructure with a striking divergence in targets: **Kotak** (ADD, FV ₹25, May-2026) and **Motilal Oswal** (Buy, TP ₹52, Feb-2026) — a near-2x gap against a CMP of roughly ₹23. Both are constructive, but the magnitude of disagreement is unusual. Kotak carries an explicit **sector-cautious** lens on roads yet still rates IRB ADD, indicating stock-specific merit; its ₹25 FV implies single-digit upside and has moved only marginally (₹24→₹25) even after a 26% PAT beat in Q4FY26. MO upgraded to Buy in Nov-2025 (from Neutral, TP ₹50→₹52) and has held that stance; its ₹52 target almost certainly reflects a sum-of-parts NAV approach that capitalises long-duration TOT concession cash flows at a lower discount rate than Kotak's. The central debate is whether IRB's recent TOT-17/18 wins represent durable value creation (MO's view) or expensive bets that will weigh on the balance sheet and dilute near-term returns (Kotak's implicit caution).

My own read: IRB is the only private operator in India with meaningful scale in both BOT and TOT assets, which gives it structural advantages in government tender eligibility and operating leverage on toll O&M. That said, the ₹25-vs-₹52 spread should prompt scrutiny rather than confidence — the market at ₹23 is effectively rejecting both targets, and the most likely reason is balance-sheet risk: project-level debt across SPVs, acquisition-cost risk on TOT bundles priced in a competitive window, and the government's track record on toll-rate revisions. The Q4FY26 PAT beat was partly a lower-tax-rate tailwind — not a clean margin story. I'd anchor closer to Kotak's conservative FV near term and treat the MO target as the upside scenario conditional on (a) TOT-17/18 delivering in-line or better traffic ramp, and (b) no fresh capital raise at dilutive terms. The single most important watch item is traffic volume on newly acquired TOTs versus acquisition-time underwriting assumptions.

Kotak|260522.change: PT raised ₹24→₹25; ADD maintained. No change in rating; sector view remains Cautious.
Kotak|260522.view:
Kotak's ADD against a cautious sector backdrop is a guarded endorsement — it signals conviction on IRB's relative merits (TOT pipeline, PAT beat) without enthusiasm for the sector. The ₹1 PT lift is minimal and implies the 26% PAT beat was not enough to materially re-rate the stock: Kotak is likely discounting the tax-rate benefit as non-recurring and maintaining conservatism on TOT acquisition value.

The call is credible precisely because it is restrained. What I'd watch: does Kotak raise the FV more meaningfully once TOT-17 and TOT-18 traffic data is visible (typically 6–12 months post-takeover)? If yes, that would signal the cautious case is unwinding. If the FV stays pinned near ₹25, it likely reflects persistent concern about leverage or the quality of future TOT bundle pricing.

MO|260216.change: TP ₹52 maintained; Buy maintained. Unchanged from MO's Nov-2025 upgrade note (when TP moved ₹50→₹52 and rating was upgraded from Neutral to Buy).
MO|260216.view:
MO's ₹52 target is striking — it is more than double Kotak's FV and roughly 2.3x the CMP at time of publication. This level of premium over the market price typically reflects a NAV-based model that assigns significant option value to pipeline wins and applies an aggressive discount rate to long-duration toll cash flows. The structural bull case is coherent: TOT assets have inflation-linked tariff revision clauses, traffic historically compounds at 6–8% on national highways, and a well-run operator like IRB can extract operating-cost efficiencies at scale.

However, the market's persistent discount to even Kotak's ₹25 target (let alone MO's ₹52) suggests investors are not giving full credit to either NAV or near-term EPS. I would stress-test two assumptions in MO's model: (1) the traffic growth rate assumed for TOT-17/18 — if these were acquired at peak competitive pricing, the margin of safety is thin; (2) the debt cost embedded in the NAV — rising rates or refinancing risk across SPVs can compress NAV non-linearly. MO's ₹52 is the bull-case ceiling, not a base case, until project-level debt is demonstrably on a downward trajectory.

ITC.summary:
**Kotak's Jun 2026 upgrade to Buy** (PT ₹365) is the defining change to the ITC picture. The house that was the most analytically rigorous bear post-Q4 — explicitly flagging GST methodology noise and one-off realisation gains — has flipped to the bull side on valuation grounds, leaving the current line-up as: 2 bulls (**CLSA** OP ₹394, **Kotak** Buy ₹365), 4 neutrals (**Axis** Hold ₹380 stale, **ICICI Direct** Hold ₹385 stale, **Jefferies** Hold ₹350, **JPMorgan** Neutral ₹325), and 2 bears (**Nomura** Reduce ₹300, **PL** Reduce ₹302). The ₹94 spread (floor ₹300 to ceiling ₹394) remains wide, and Kotak's Buy at ₹365 sitting below CLSA's OP at ₹394 signals that even the bulls are valuation-anchored rather than conviction-driven. The core debate is unchanged: will 1QFY27 cigarette volume data show the excise hike caused lasting structural damage (Nomura/PL thesis) or a transitional dislocation that calibrated pricing and mix normalises through FY27 (Kotak/CLSA thesis)? Note that Axis (₹380) and ICICI Direct (₹385) are January 2026 pre-shock downgrade notes — their seemingly high targets are stale anchors, not current views.

My own read: Kotak's upgrade is the most important signal in this cycle — not because it confirms operational recovery (1QFY27 will settle that), but because the most rigorous bear just said the stock has become cheap enough to buy. That tends to mark a near-term floor. That said, I'd be cautious about reading too much fundamental conviction into a valuation-driven flip: Kotak accepted ongoing EBIT headwinds explicitly. The cigarette franchise is durable — ITC has navigated every excise cycle and eventually passes through pricing — but the FY26 Budget hike was steeper and faster than prior cycles, and illicit-trade substitution is the non-linear risk the bulls consistently underweight. I'd stay neutrally constructive pending 1QFY27 data. The single number to watch: cigarette volume — any decline beyond low-single-digits on a comparable basis is a structural red flag. If volumes hold, Kotak's valuation call looks well-timed.

CLSA|260522.change: No prior CLSA report in the library to compare (prevTP null); PT ₹394, Outperform — first captured CLSA note for ITC.
CLSA|260522.view:
CLSA is the lone unambiguous bull, anchoring on the 15% cigarette EBIT beat vs consensus and full-year net revenue growth of 8.2%. Their OP thesis implicitly requires 4Q to have been a clean beat rather than a pipeline-distorted one — that is the key assumption to stress-test. The PT of ₹394 sits well above every other house in the pack, including the other neutrals, suggesting CLSA is pricing in a faster-than-consensus normalisation.

I'd give CLSA partial credit: the EBIT beat is real, and management's interventions (staggered pricing, Long-segment push) are sensible. But the absence of a prior report means we can't see whether they had already baked in some of this optimism pre-results. Worth watching whether they maintain OP after the 1QFY27 print.

JP|260522.view:
JPMorgan's note is the most balanced in the set — acknowledging the 3% EBITDA beat while pinning the investment case on 1QFY27 clarity. The unchanged PT and rating reflect genuine agnosticism: they're not chasing the beat nor panicking on the excise headwind. Their enumeration of ITC's defensive levers (staggered price hikes, new SKUs, Long-segment) is useful colour — it shows management is taking the illicit-trade risk seriously, which is actually somewhat reassuring.

The Neutral at ₹325 implies meaningful downside from the bear scenario. I'd give this note reasonable weight as a calibrated fence-sit; the signal to watch from JP's frame is whether those defensive levers show up in 1Q channel data.

Nomura|260522.view:
Nomura holds the street's lowest PT at ₹300, and their technical point about the GST computation methodology change is important — it's not just about demand optics, it means the base comparison is legally/structurally different, making even internal trend analysis unreliable for 4Q. This is a more serious analytical issue than the market is generally pricing.

A ₹300 target implies they're positioning for a downside scenario in 1QFY27, not a central one. That feels like the bearish tail rather than the base case, but if volumes disappoint materially — say, cigarette vol down 5–8% — Nomura looks prescient. I'd treat ₹300 as a stress-case anchor rather than a central estimate, but the comparability argument is worth taking seriously when reading 1Q numbers.

Jeff|260521.view:
Jefferies made the largest absolute PT reduction in this cycle (₹50), bringing them from the most optimistic neutral to roughly mid-pack. The title 'Now is The Real Test' captures the consensus anxiety cleanly. Hold at ₹350 is a fence-sitting position — they've reset their bull scenario but haven't committed to Reduce. Their framing that 4Q 'likely benefited from pipeline inventory around the cut-off date' aligns with Kotak's noise argument.

If 1QFY27 volumes hold, Jefferies will look too cautious; if they disappoint, they'll likely join the reduce camp. The ₹350 PT lands between JP's ₹325 and Axis's ₹380, and I think it's the most honest statement of where informed uncertainty sits right now.

PL|260521.change: No pdfdata entry for this note; trendlyne shows Reduce/Sell call, PT ₹302, dated May 2026.
PL|260521.view:
PL's note is the thinnest in the set — the houseView paragraph is essentially just the headline, with no analytical reasoning available in the library. Their PT of ₹302 is effectively at Nomura's floor, implying a similar downside scenario. Without the underlying analysis, it's hard to evaluate whether this is a well-grounded bear case or directional momentum-following.

I'd treat PL as a directional flag — confirming the bear camp has multiple constituents — rather than an analytically independent data point. If they publish a fuller note post-1Q, it would be worth reading to see if the reasoning holds up.

Axis|260105.change: Downgraded to Hold from prior Buy (per trendlyne), PT ₹380, dated January 2026. No post-Q4FY26 update in the library.
Axis|260105.view:
This is a stale pre-results note from January 2026, five months before Q4 earnings. The Axis downgrade was part of the broad consumer/FMCG de-rating at the start of the year, likely reflecting slowing urban consumption and valuation concerns — before the excise-hike story fully crystallised. Their ₹380 PT is the second-highest in the pack, which almost certainly reflects a pre-shock price anchor rather than a current active view.

Without a post-Q4 update, this note's signal value is limited to 'they were cautious enough to cut Buy in January.' I'd discount it heavily in forming a current view and flag that the ₹380 target is probably stale by at least one revision cycle.

ICICI|260102.change: Downgraded to Hold from prior Buy (per trendlyne), PT ₹385, dated January 2026. No post-Q4FY26 update in the library.
ICICI|260102.view:
Essentially the same vintage and story as Axis — a January 2026 downgrade reflecting sector caution before Q4 results, with the highest PT in the current set (₹385) suggesting the view hasn't been updated for the excise-hike impact. That both Axis and ICICI are sitting on stale January notes without post-Q4 revisions is itself a data point: they may have less conviction in either direction, or their updates simply aren't in the local library yet.

I'd treat the ₹385 as an outdated pre-shock anchor. If either house publishes a post-Q4 note, that will be the one worth reading — their January downgrade provides no read-through to current fundamentals.

Kotak|260615.change: Upgraded to Buy from Reduce; PT raised ₹330→₹365 (Jun 2026).
Kotak|260615.view:
This is a valuation-driven upgrade, not a fundamental view change. Kotak explicitly titled the note "Upgrade to BUY on favorable valuations," accepting that EBIT headwinds from the cigarette tax pass-through (partial pricing absorption, adverse consumer mix shift from KSFT/RSFT toward Longs) are real but time-limited, and that the stock's de-rating has made the risk-reward attractive. The PT of ₹365 — only ₹35 above the prior Reduce target of ₹330 — signals caution, not enthusiasm.

The most notable aspect of this flip is its context: Kotak was arguably the most rigorous bear in May 2026, calling out one-off realisation gains and GST methodology changes that made 4Q unreadable. They have not retracted that analysis — they have simply decided the price now compensates for the uncertainty. That is a disciplined, valuation-anchored stance rather than a thesis reversal. Watch whether they maintain Buy through the 1QFY27 print, which is the real test their May note identified.

ITC Hotels.summary:
**Jefferies** is the only broker covering ITC Hotels in our library, maintaining a Buy at ₹205 PT after a marginal cut from ₹210 following weak Q4FY26 results. The weakness was driven by Foreign Tourist Arrival (FTA) disruptions affecting South India assets in March; 1QFY27 is expected to recover. There is no cross-house debate in our data — coverage is thin, reflecting ITC Hotels' recent demerger status.

**My own read:** ITC Hotels owns some of India's most irreplaceable hospitality assets — the Maurya (Delhi), Rajputana (Jaipur), Grand Chola (Chennai), Sonar (Kolkata). The FTA disruption is transitory; the structural thesis is owned-RevPAR recovery as international travel normalises. The FY26 demerger from ITC Ltd means institutional coverage is still building — the relatively thin sell-side base is itself an opportunity. The Sri Lanka hotel improving occupancy and the new 72-key Kerala acquisition are early signs of post-demerger capital deployment. Key watches: (1) owned RevPAR trajectory as FTA normalises in 2QFY27, (2) capex discipline — the company must demonstrate it can grow without destroying returns, and (3) whether an asset-light layer develops over time. At ₹205, Jefferies calls valuations reasonable; I'd agree the franchise quality justifies a premium, but the light coverage means price discovery is incomplete.

Jeff|260517.change: PT lowered ₹210→₹205; Buy maintained. Weak Q4FY26 (3% owned RevPAR growth, negative operating leverage) due to FTA disruption in South India; FY27 capex estimate raised for Kerala acquisition.
Jeff|260517.view:
Jefferies is constructive on the quality of the franchise and sees the FTA impact as transitory — 1QFY27 should improve and the Sri Lanka hotel is gaining occupancy. The marginal PT cut is pragmatic rather than a change in thesis; the Buy is maintained on what the note describes as reasonable valuations.

The call is credible. Jefferies is the most active institutional voice in Indian hospitality, and this is an initiating-style note on a freshly demerged company. I'd stress-test the 'reasonable valuations' claim — ITC Hotels' owned-asset model carries higher depreciation/capex than asset-light peers, which compresses FCF. Watch whether Jefferies revisits the PT upward once FTA data normalises, and monitor the Kerala acquisition's economics on disclosure.

Indian Hotels.summary:
Four houses cover **Indian Hotels**, all bullish. **Nomura** (Jun-2026, BUY, PT ₹800 maintained) is now the freshest voice — its 4QFY26 earnings review shows EBITDA growth of 12%/9% y-y with a strong Jan-Feb followed by March disruptions, and expects a strong 2HFY27. **Jefferies** (May-2026, no PT in this sector/monitor note) is tracking monthly RevPAR data and called IHCL its top pick in Hotels; April RevPAR rebounded to ~8% YoY after a weak March, constructive for the thesis. **Motilal Oswal** (Feb-2026, Buy, TP ₹900) and **ICICI Securities** (Jul-2025, Buy, TP ₹941) are the staler voices. The TP range is striking: ICICI ₹941 (stale, Jul-2025) → MO ₹900 (Feb-2026) → Nomura ₹800 (Jun-2026); the most current estimate is meaningfully below the older ones. No bear voice sits in our library, though a Morgan Stanley note on Indian Hotels Company from Jun-2026 (EW, TP ₹783, not in our houseViews) provides the cautious counterpoint. The real debate is whether the FTA-disruption-driven March RevPAR dip was transient — April's bounce supports that case — or whether Nomura's more conservative ₹800 PT reflects a more structural international demand shortfall.

**My own read:** IHCL's Taj franchise is genuinely the strongest luxury hospitality brand in India — pricing power in gateway cities is durable, and the Ginger rollout gives volume optionality most Indian hotel chains lack. The risk the sell-side is underweighting: IHCL has been trading at 35–40x EV/EBITDA, well above global hospitality comps, and the 11–14% EBITDA CAGR the bulls project is respectable but not exceptional enough to justify that multiple if rates stay elevated. Nomura's ₹800 is now the active anchor I'd respect — it is fresher than the ₹900/₹941 targets and aligns more closely with the Morgan Stanley EW at ₹783. I'd watch: (1) whether 2HFY27 ADR recovery materialises as Nomura expects; (2) new luxury supply from Marriott/Hilton threatening metro RevPAR premiums; (3) Ginger brand economics showing up in ROCE; and (4) balance sheet discipline as capex intensity rises.

Nomura|260615.change: PT ₹800 maintained; BUY maintained (unchanged vs prior Nomura report in pdfdata).
Nomura|260615.view:
Nomura's 4QFY26 earnings review is the freshest data point in our coverage. The pattern — strong Jan-Feb, disrupted March — confirms what April RevPAR data (Jefferies) also showed: domestic demand is resilient but the international mix shortfall hit premium ADR realizations. "War-related volatility giving opportunity" frames the dip as transient; the "strong 2HFY27" call is the base case the entire bullish cohort shares.

Nomura's ₹800 PT is notably below Motilal Oswal (₹900) and ICICI (₹941), despite being the most current note — implying Nomura is baking in a more modest ADR recovery trajectory or a tighter multiple. I'd anchor to Nomura's current estimate as the most reliable active figure in the set; the higher targets have not been refreshed post the FTA disruption and risk being stale.

Jeff|260519.change: Sector/monitor note — no TP or rating disclosed in this report; pdfdata confirms null TP/call. No prior report in pdfdata to compare.
Jeff|260519.view:
Jefferies is using monthly RevPAR data to track the thesis in real time — April's ~8% YoY print validates their base case of re-accelerating growth after a disrupted March. Calling IHCL "top pick in Hotels" is a strong conviction signal from a broker with serious Indian hospitality coverage depth.

This note is best read as thesis-confirming rather than thesis-setting. The 7–8% RevPAR CAGR and 11–14% EBITDA CAGR assumptions are the numbers to hold Jefferies to over the next two years. If metro RevPAR growth stalls below 5% for two consecutive quarters, that would be the key trigger to revisit the call.

MO|260212.change: Trendlyne: Buy, TP ₹900 (Feb-2026). No prior Trendlyne entry to compare; dated ~4 months ago.
MO|260212.view:
Motilal Oswal's "diversification and scale" framing captures the multi-brand strategy (Taj, Vivanta, SeleQtions, Ginger) that insulates IHCL from any single segment slowdown. The Feb-2026 note is now 4 months old but the core thesis is intact given April RevPAR data.

TP ₹900 vs Nomura's more recent ₹800 is a meaningful gap. MO's Buy is credible but arguably consensus — worth watching whether they revisit the TP post-4QFY26 results and whether the model explicitly incorporates Ginger's expanding unit economics.

ICICI|250718.change: Trendlyne: Buy, TP ₹941 (Jul-2025). No prior Trendlyne entry to compare; note is 11 months stale.
ICICI|250718.view:
The Jul-2025 note ("Resilience amid turbulence") was written before the FTA disruptions and April's RevPAR bounce, making it the stalest view in coverage. TP ₹941 should be treated as obsolete — the macro and competitive picture has shifted enough that this number is unreliable as a current estimate.

Discount this view heavily. If ICICI has not refreshed since July 2025, the specific TP is not actionable. The directional bullish stance is probably still correct, but the magnitude is stale.

Indian Oil Corporation.summary:
The house spread on **IOCL** is unusually wide and has been shifting toward caution since the 4QFY26 results. **Nomura** (Buy, PT ₹180 — designating IOCL its top pick among OMCs) and **Jefferies** (Buy, PT ₹175) anchor the bull case, joined by **JPMorgan** (OW; First Take held PT at ₹200, but a same-day fuller note cut to ₹170) and **BOB** (upgraded to Buy, PT ₹173). **PL** sits at Accumulate (PT ₹145). Moving to neutral: **CLSA** maintained Hold but cut PT sharply from ₹150 to ₹135 — essentially at CMP — and flagged IOCL's decision to withhold GRM/inventory disclosure as making the bull case hard to underwrite; **Geojit** went further, downgrading from Buy (PT ₹179, Jan-2026) to Hold (PT ₹153, May-2026). **Kotak** stands alone as a Sell (FV ₹120), forecasting large 1HFY27 losses. The 4QFY26 beat (PAT ~₹114bn, up 57% YoY; EBITDA up 53% YoY) was broadly acknowledged as inventory-driven; the debate has shifted entirely to how deep 1HFY27 gets. PT range: ₹120 (Kotak) to ₹175–₹180 (bulls), with JPMorgan's effective target at ₹170 despite the First Take's ₹200 placeholder.

My own read: The 4QFY26 beat flatters a structurally challenged business. Marketing margins on petrol and diesel remain sharply negative — Jefferies flagged double-digit ₹/litre losses — and the real swing variable is government fuel-price policy, not GRM cycles or capacity ramp timelines. IOCL's withholding of GRM and inventory-gain breakdown is a significant governance concern that the bulls are too ready to dismiss. Kotak's 1HFY27 loss scenario is the most rigorous forecast and is consistent with the macro backdrop: higher crude premiums, shipping cost inflation, and a weaker rupee all compound standalone margin pressure. The refinery expansion upside (commissioning 2HCY26, real gains from 2028 per CLSA) is distant and already embedded in the bull models. At ~₹135 CMP with near-term losses likely and disclosure opacity high, I lean closer to CLSA and Geojit than to the buy camp. The single catalyst that would change the picture dramatically — a fuel price hike — is politically constrained. Key watchpoints: any fuel-price-hike announcement, 1QFY27 results, crude import premium trajectory.

Geojit|260525.change: Downgraded from Buy to Hold; PT ₹179→₹153 (vs Jan-2026 prior in trendlyne). No pdfdata match for this report.
Geojit|260525.view: Geojit's trajectory on IOCL has been reactive: they upgraded to Buy at ₹179 in January 2026 near the post-correction high, then downgraded to Hold at ₹153 in May once conditions deteriorated — the opposite of prescient. That said, Hold at ₹153 vs ~₹135 CMP is at least honest about limited near-term catalysts. I would treat this as a trailing signal rather than a leading one; the timing pattern suggests Geojit follows macro developments rather than anticipating them.

CLSA|260520.view: CLSA's Hold with a PT at CMP is the most candid neutral in the set. They flagged two things the bulls are glossing over: IOCL's withholding of GRM and inventory-gain disclosure makes the 4Q beat unverifiable on a fundamental basis, and the refinery-expansion gains will not materialise until 2028 — a very long wait for a cyclical PSU. A ₹135 PT implies zero upside from current prices, effectively a "hold what you have, do not add." I find CLSA's scepticism well-grounded. If 1QFY27 results confirm the marketing-loss trajectory Kotak models, CLSA's PT will look prudent in retrospect.

PL|260520.change: Accumulate maintained; PT ₹152→₹145 (vs Aug-2025 prior in trendlyne). No pdfdata match for this report.
PL|260520.view: PL's Accumulate at ₹145 sits in a no-man's land — above Hold conviction but well below the bull camp's ₹175–₹180 targets. At ~₹135 CMP, ₹145 implies only ~7% upside, which hardly justifies an Accumulate unless you expect a near-term catalyst (fuel price hike). The framing — "strong Q4 beat but Q1 challenging" — is accurate but the rating has not followed the logic. This reads more as a value-watch than genuine conviction; incrementally useful as confirmation that even the moderates are losing optimism on the near-term.

JP|260519.change: OW maintained; PT unchanged at ₹200 in the First Take note. JPMorgan issued a same-day fuller note cutting PT ₹200→₹170 — the effective working OW target is ₹170.
JP|260519.view: JPMorgan's First Take captured the immediate beat reaction before their analysts had processed the full details; the substantive follow-up the same day cut PT from ₹200 to ₹170. The OW case rests on IOCL's higher refining-to-marketing mix vs HPCL/BPCL, plus the petchem EBIT recovery trend — legitimate differentiators. At ₹170 OW, JPMorgan implies ~26% upside from ~₹135 CMP. Achievable if marketing losses reverse or refinery capacity additions get credited earlier than 2028, but both are dependent on either government action or a macro shift not in the near-term base case.

Jeff|260519.view: Jefferies maintains Buy on the valuation argument — "1 SD below historical mean" — while simultaneously cataloguing structural headwinds: sharply negative marketing margins, high crude premiums, freight cost inflation, rupee depreciation, and expanding working capital. That combination of bullish rating alongside a bearish macro description is internally inconsistent unless the valuation discount is believed to more than compensate for all of it. I would stress-test the mean-reversion assumption: if 1HFY27 losses materialise as Kotak projects, the historical mean shifts and the valuation comfort erodes. The PT cut from ₹185 to ₹175 is a calibrated acknowledgment of deteriorating conditions — reasonable, but I would want to see 1QFY27 before endorsing the Buy with conviction.

Kotak|260519.change: Sell maintained; FV raised ₹100→₹120. Stock at ~₹135 CMP remains above their fair value.
Kotak|260519.view: Kotak's is the most rigorous bear case and, paradoxically, even they raised their FV after the 4Q beat — from ₹100 to ₹120 — implying the results were genuinely better than feared even by a Sell-side analyst. But ₹120 FV vs ₹135 CMP still implies 11% downside, and the thesis (large 1HFY27 losses from negative marketing margins and macro disruption) is well-supported: GRM opacity, crude premium headwinds, and the historical pattern of OMC earnings being hostage to fuel pricing policy all point the same direction. I regard Kotak's near-term scenario as the most honest forecast in the set. The Sell will look right if Q1FY27 delivers the losses they model — and Kotak will be the one house that did not get caught off guard by the results optics.

Nomura|260519.change: Buy maintained; PT ₹190→₹180. Nomura designates IOCL top pick among OMCs.
Nomura|260519.view: Nomura's "top pick among OMCs" is a relative, not absolute, call: they believe IOCL's greater refining exposure gives it an edge over the more marketing-heavy HPCL and BPCL when product cracks are more visible than marketing margins. That relative case is legitimate. The PT cut from ₹190 to ₹180 is modest, suggesting Nomura's model is relatively insensitive to the 1HFY27 loss scenario Kotak outlines. The ₹180 target (~33% upside from ~₹135) requires either marketing margin recovery or the market crediting refinery expansion well ahead of commissioning. The "top pick" designation is most useful for OMC relative positioning, not as a standalone buy argument in a sector with near-term earnings headwinds.

BOB|260519.change: Upgraded from Hold to Buy; PT cut ₹181→₹173 (vs Feb-2026 prior in trendlyne). No pdfdata match for this report.
BOB|260519.view: BOB's simultaneous upgrade (Hold→Buy) and PT cut (₹181→₹173) is a classic "fallen enough to own" call — driven by price action rather than fundamental improvement. The logic is simple: after a significant de-rating, the risk/reward improves even as the intrinsic estimate edges down. Mechanically sound but not particularly insightful; there is no discernible differentiated thesis here relative to Jefferies or Nomura. Adds to the bullish headcount without meaningfully strengthening the bull case's quality.

Indigo Paints.summary:
The **Indigo Paints** coverage set has a severe staleness problem. The only fresh view is **Kotak**'s Reduce (PT ₹900, May-2026) following 4QFY26 results — a Reduce but with PT raised from ₹850, as decorative growth of 8.5% YoY was marginally better than feared. The bulls — **ICICI** (Buy, PT ₹1200, Feb-2026) and **Motilal Oswal** (Buy, PT ₹1400, Nov-2025) — are 4–7 months old and built on a recovery thesis that Kotak's fresher data does not confirm. **Asit** (Hold, PT ₹1710, Nov-2024) and **Keynote** (Neutral/downgrade, PT ₹1457, Aug-2024) are 19–22 months old and can be disregarded for current analysis. The central debate — between Kotak's Reduce at ₹900 and ICICI/MO's stale Buys at ₹1200–₹1400 — hinges on whether Indigo can re-accelerate to its stated 1.5–2× industry growth, something it has not delivered in recent quarters. Kotak's core critique: 8.5% decorative growth is "a tad better than peers" but well below Indigo's own target; EBITDA margin flat at 22.5% despite 180bp of gross margin expansion, fully offset by sales-force and A&P investment.

My own read: Indigo is a quality franchise that has lost its growth-premium narrative. The differentiated product moat — Dirtproof, Bright Ceiling, Floor-Guard, Apple Chemie — is real but not wide enough to consistently outgrow Asian Paints, Berger, and Kansai in a price-competitive decorative market. The EBITDA margin story tells it plainly: the company is reinvesting the entire input-cost tailwind into distribution and branding — necessary, but not yet converting to sustained volume acceleration. Apple Chemie (industrial/construction chemicals), which ICICI highlights as a bull driver, is genuinely interesting — less commoditised, better pricing power — but currently too small to move consolidated results. Kotak's ₹900 Reduce implies the market is right to reprice away from a "premium-growth" multiple toward an "in-line growth at a discount" multiple, and I agree with that framework. Until Indigo demonstrates two consecutive quarters of 1.5×+ industry growth, the re-rating story is on hold. Key watchpoints: (1) quarterly decorative volume growth vs peers; (2) Apple Chemie revenue disclosed separately and growing meaningfully.

Kotak|260526.view: Kotak's Reduce with a raised PT is a grudging acknowledgment that 4QFY26 was marginally less bad than feared — 8.5% decorative growth was "a tad better than peers." But the core critique is intact: Indigo has positioned itself as a 1.5–2× industry grower, and barely matching industry pace means the premium multiple is unjustified. The structural concern is the EBITDA margin: 180bp of GM expansion fully offset by opex investment shows the growth machine is still burning fuel to maintain speed rather than accelerating. The Reduce at a PT only modestly above (or at) CMP signals Kotak sees better value elsewhere in the consumer space. This is the most credible and current view in the set, and I weight it accordingly.

ICICI|260215.change: Buy (upgraded at some point vs Hold in May-2024 prior); PT ₹1380→₹1200. No pdfdata match; no intermediate ICICI entry in library between May-2024 and Feb-2026.
ICICI|260215.view: ICICI's Feb-2026 Buy at ₹1200 is primarily anchored to Apple Chemie's strong performance and broader market-share gains. The PT cut from ₹1380 to ₹1200 reflects lower estimates after the stock's significant decline — a "fallen enough to own" call. ICICI's track record on this name has been inconsistent (Sell in 2023, Hold in 2024, Buy in 2026), which tempers conviction. At ~4 months old, this note predates Kotak's May-2026 data showing growth in line with — not ahead of — peers. I would want an updated ICICI note post-4QFY26 results before treating the ₹1200 Buy as actionable.

MO|251108.change: Buy maintained; PT ₹1400 unchanged (vs Aug-2025 prior in trendlyne).
MO|251108.view: MO's Nov-2025 Buy at ₹1400 is ~7 months old and the "recovery momentum building, positive 2H outlook" thesis has not been vindicated by Kotak's May-2026 data. Indraprastha Gas.summary:
**JPMorgan** is the lone bear at UW (PT ₹120, cut from ₹125), citing sequential gross-margin compression to ₹10.9/SCM, a weak gas-purchase mix shift, and a 21% YoY PAT decline in 4QFY26. All other houses are constructive: **CLSA** (O-PF, PT ₹210 cut from ₹240) and **Nomura** (BUY, PT ₹200, first captured report) anchor the bull camp; **Jefferies** is BUY at ₹180 (cut from ₹205); **BOB Capital** BUY at ₹184 (cut from ₹197); **Prabhudas Lilladhar** Accumulate at ₹191 (upgraded from Sell in Feb 2026). **Kotak** is the dissenting local at REDUCE/₹160 — a fresh initiation, the lowest non-JP PT — while **Geojit** sits at Hold/₹173 (upgraded from Sell in Mar 2026). Target spread is wide: ₹120–₹210. CLSA explicitly models margins “much lower than guided,” and Jefferies uses a conservative 5% volume CAGR, so even the bulls embed a discount to management’s double-digit volume + ₹7–8/scm EBITDA guidance. The real debate is whether the CNG-bus retirement drag in Delhi is truly behind and whether APM gas input costs have bottomed.

My own read: IGL has genuine toll-road quality — near-monopoly CGA in Delhi NCR, decades of PNG conversion runway, sticky industrial and commercial volumes. The franchise is not in dispute; the margin structure is. The core risk is that IGL sits downstream of an opaque APM gas allocation policy: if the government trims allocations or prices market gas higher, ₹7–8/scm EBITDA/scm is aspirational, not structural. JPMorgan’s ₹120 looks too punitive — it doesn’t credit the franchise or any recovery — but Kotak’s REDUCE at ₹160 is the right discipline check. I’d be closest to Jefferies (BUY, ₹180) with the caveat that the PT is conditional on FY27 volume recovering as the Delhi bus fleet transitions. The two things I’d watch: (1) APM gas allocation volumes and whether IGL’s share shrinks further in FY27; (2) CNG retail volume momentum in 1QFY27 — the first clean quarter post-bus retirement.

CLSA|260520.change: PT lowered ₹240→₹210; O-PF (Outperform) maintained. FY27/28 EPS cut 14%/9%.
CLSA|260520.view: CLSA is the highest-PT bull but is trimming estimates aggressively, acknowledging that 4QFY26’s 34% PAT beat was real but driven partly by better-than-modelled margins — not a run-rate base. Their most important signal is the explicit statement that they model “much lower than guided” on both margins and volume growth. That is a credible research stance: management’s ₹7–8/scm target is medium-term, not near-term deliverable. The ₹210 PT (even after the cut) implies CLSA is buying the franchise at a discount, expecting eventual margin normalisation. Reasonable, but the downside scenario — a sustained APM gas cost headwind — is not fully reflected even at ₹210. The O-PF is a comfortable hold, not a high-conviction buy.

JP|260520.view: JP is the structural bear, and their thesis — sequential margin compression, gas-mix headwinds, INR pressure — is factually grounded in 4Q data. But ₹120 as fair value goes well beyond a near-term margin dip: it implies permanent impairment of the franchise. For a CGD monopoly with mandated geographic exclusivity, that seems too aggressive. JP is right to flag the ₹11.1→₹10.9/SCM gross-margin compression and the HH gas mix shift, but their PT appears to embed both sustained cost escalation and zero pricing power recovery. Use JP’s note to stress-test margin assumptions, not to set a price target.

Nomura|260520.change: First captured Nomura report on IGL (prevTP null, no prior to compare); PT ₹200, BUY.
Nomura|260520.view: Nomura enters with BUY/₹200 — close to CLSA — acknowledging a 3% EBITDA miss vs their forecast but a 5% consensus beat. Their cost concerns (staff 11% above estimate, raw material 5% above) are consistent with the broader picture. The report title “volume may surprise” signals they see upside optionality in volume recovery. At ₹200, Nomura is broadly aligned with the bull camp on franchise value. As a first-captured report there is no track record to judge how responsive their estimates are to misses; the ₹200 target may be more of an initiation anchor than a conviction level.

Jeff|260519.view: Jefferies shows measured discipline: they cut the PT ~12% while holding BUY, and their 5% volume CAGR assumption (FY26–28E) is deliberately below management’s double-digit guidance. The key call is that the CNG-bus retirement drag in Delhi is now behind — which, if correct, turns FY27 into a cleaner volume recovery year. The ₹180 target is the most conservative among the BUY camp, making it the most credible entry point. The PT trim is a proper acknowledgment that prior estimates had been too optimistic. This is one of the more trustworthy notes in the set.

Kotak|260519.change: First captured Kotak report on IGL (prevCall null, no prior to compare); PT ₹160, REDUCE initiated.
Kotak|260519.view: Kotak’s REDUCE at ₹160 is the most bearish domestic call. Despite acknowledging the 4Q EBITDA beat (10.5% above their estimate), the 15.4% QoQ EBITDA decline and EBITDA/scm compression to ₹4.9 dominate their assessment. The report title “CNG price increases getting easier” hints that Kotak’s upgrade scenario requires retail tariff hikes that are not yet certain. A REDUCE with the stock likely 10–20% above ₹160 is a contrarian call that will be validated or disproven quickly in 1QFY27. Worth watching whether Kotak revises upward after any CNG price hike.

BOB|260519.change: PT cut ₹197→₹184 (based on trendlyne history; Feb 2026 BOB entry had PT ₹197); BUY maintained.
BOB|260519.view: BOB Capital’s BUY at ₹184 is a middle-ground call — acknowledging the operational miss on higher costs while keeping faith in the recovery thesis. The ₹184 PT clusters with the cautious-but-constructive camp (PL Accumulate ₹191, Geojit Hold ₹173). This is a trendlyne-sourced external call; without the full report it is harder to assess the rigour of the estimate revision. Take the PT cut as a directional signal rather than a precise valuation update.
